By incorporating this newly discovered sample, we refined the model's performance, achieving a 91% precision for Seyfert 1.9 classification. These findings confirm the model's ability to isolate Seyfert 1.9 spectra within a Seyfert 2 population. Furthermore, we decomposed the H$\alpha$ emission lines of the identified Seyfert 1.9 galaxies using a two-Gaussian fit to derive line widths and fluxes. Analysis of the broad H$\alpha$ component in the new sample revealed a velocity distribution with an extended tail toward higher velocities and a luminosity slightly lower than that of the original sample, indicating that the model successfully isolates sources with relatively weak broad H$\alpha$ components. Additionally, we examined the host galaxy morphology distributions and found that the new sample is predominantly composed of galaxies with large bulges. Finally, we release an online catalog containing 1,297 Seyfert 1.9 galaxies, complete with H$\alpha$ emission line measurements.

The growing popularity of Internet of Things (IoT) smart home applications has inadvertently increased malicious activity, driving a high demand for cost-effective security solutions. This paper introduces a low-end architectural design to enhance home network security by integrating private blockchain technology with RSSI-based trilateration for localization. We evaluated the advantages of private blockchains compared to public ones and refined the localization algorithm's accuracy by testing it across various wireless technologies. The findings indicate that combining a private blockchain with a WiFi-based communication system yields the most efficient implementation of this proposed design.

Advances in gravitational wave interferometry necessitate more relevant theoretical frameworks for wave generation and propagation. While potential mechanisms for producing spin-2 spacetime perturbations remain unexplored, this study focuses on their subsequent scattering off other black holes (BHs). Specifically, we extend the Regge-Wheeler-Zerilli equations to describe distorted black holes (those surrounded by matter) within Minkowski and Anti-de Sitter spacetimes, where the metric potential satisfies the Liouville equation. We identify notable distinctions in the scattering properties of waves with varying spins and angular momenta, including gravitational waves, resulting from the loss of spherical symmetry in their propagation environment. In particular, we highlight the profound influence of background geometry deformation on grey-body factors and the absorption cross-sections of scattered waves, and we investigate the stability of the background geometry as deformation parameters vary.

We present a new category of abstract nonlinear fractional pseudo-differential equations within Banach spaces, encompassing both Mc-Kean-Vlasov equations for nonlinear Markov processes and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB)-Isaacs equations for stochastic control and games. This framework facilitates a unified examination of these equations, yielding a robust theory of coupled forward-backward systems—specifically, forward Mc-Kean-Vlasov evolution paired with backward HJB-Isaacs evolution—which are fundamental to contemporary mean-field game theory.

To explore the link between electronic band structures and ferromagnetism in SrRuO$_3$ (SRO) thin films, we conducted in-situ angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin-resolved ARPES (SARPES) measurements. Our high-quality data reveal distinct spin-split band structures. We observed that spin polarization varies significantly with momentum near the Fermi level but shows reduced dependence at higher binding energies; this aligns closely with our dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) simulations. As the temperature rises from low values to the Curie point, the spin-splitting gap narrows and band dispersions lose coherence. Combining these experimental findings with theoretical calculations, we conclude that SRO exhibits spin-dependent electron correlations, where majority spins are localized while minority spins remain itinerant. This insight clarifies the long-debated connection between ferromagnetism and electronic structure in SRO.

Hydrodynamic analyses of stellar-mass compact objects (COs) within a common envelope (CE) indicate that the accretion rate onto the CO falls several orders of magnitude below the Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton (BHL) prediction. Nevertheless, this rate remains significantly above both the Eddington limit and the threshold for neutrino-cooled accretion, defining a regime of hypercritical accretion (HCA). Given that a binary system embedded in the CE of a tertiary star accretes at a rate comparable to a single object of equivalent total mass, we suggest stellar-evolution pathways capable of generating binary black hole (BBH) systems with component masses situated within the pair-instability supernova (PISN) mass gap. Our framework relies on HCA occurring within a BBH system engulfed by the CE of a massive tertiary star. Additionally, we introduce a mass-transfer mechanism that facilitates the accumulation of mass lost by the binary onto the third star. By employing population synthesis simulations for BBH evolution alongside standard binary-interaction principles involving a tertiary star, we successfully reproduce BBH masses consistent with estimates for GW190521. Finally, we examine the massive binary system Mk34 as a potential progenitor for BBHs in the PISN gap and address the spin distribution of mergers observed in gravitational-wave catalogs.

This study investigates new physics using final states containing two oppositely charged leptons (electrons or muons), jets from b-quarks, and missing transverse momentum ($p_\mathrm{T}^\text{miss}$). The analysis utilizes 35.9 fb$^{-1}$ of proton-proton collision data at $\sqrt{s}=$ 13 TeV recorded by the CMS detector in 2016. Requirements on $p_\mathrm{T}^\text{miss}$ and transverse mass effectively distinguish potential signals from the dominant $\mathrm{t}\overline{\mathrm{t}}$ background, with no significant deviations from background expectations observed. Exclusion limits are established within simplified supersymmetric models involving pair-produced top squarks. For top squarks decaying solely into a top quark and a neutralino, 95% confidence level limits exclude the lightest top squark mass up to 800 GeV and the lightest neutralino mass up to 360 GeV. When combined with single-lepton and all-jet channel results, these limits extend to 1050 GeV for the lightest top squark and 500 GeV for the lightest neutralino. In scenarios where top squarks decay via a cascade through charginos and sleptons, the exclusion reach extends to 1300 GeV for top squarks and 800 GeV for the lightest neutralino. Additionally, results are interpreted using a simplified dark matter model featuring a top-quark coupled scalar or pseudoscalar mediator. For light dark matter, mediator masses up to 100 GeV (scalar) and 50 GeV (pseudoscalar) are excluded, with the scalar mediator result representing some of the tightest constraints to date for this model.

Client-server sessions utilize a variation of the standard interpretation of linear logic propositions as session types, specifically employing coexponentials rather than conventional exponentials to type non-linear channels. These channels govern interactions between a group of clients and a solitary server. Coexponentials facilitate the modeling of racing interactions, where multiple clients compete for access to a single server whose internal state—and consequently, the services provided—evolve sequentially as it processes requests. This work introduces a fair termination theorem for CSLL$^\infty$, a foundational calculus for client-server sessions. We define a type system ensuring that every well-typed term maps to a valid derivation within $\mu$MALL$^\infty$, the infinitary proof theory of linear logic incorporating least and greatest fixed points. Furthermore, we demonstrate a correspondence between reductions in the calculus and principal reductions in $\mu$MALL$^\infty$. Consequently, fair termination in CSLL$^\infty$ is derived from cut elimination in $\mu$MALL$^\infty$.

Distributed optimization plays a pivotal role in various emerging fields, including robust sensor network control, smart grid management, machine learning, resource slicing, and localization. Nevertheless, the heavy reliance on data exchange between local and central nodes often leads to significant communication bottlenecks. To address this, over-the-air computing (AirComp) emerges as a promising medium access technology; by leveraging the superposition property of the wireless multiple access channel (MAC), it delivers substantial bandwidth efficiency. This study introduces an AirComp framework tailored for general distributed convex optimization problems. Specifically, the optimization process employs a distributed primal-dual (DPD) subgradient method. Under standard assumptions, we demonstrate that the DPDAirComp approach can asymptotically achieve zero expected constraint violation. Consequently, DPD-AirComp guarantees the feasibility of the original problem even in the presence of channel fading and additive noise. Furthermore, by implementing appropriate power control for user signals, the expected non-zero optimality gap can be effectively reduced. We illustrate two practical implementations of this framework: smart grid management and wireless resource allocation. Finally, numerical simulations validate the superior performance of DPDAirComp, revealing that it converges approximately one order of magnitude faster than digital orthogonal multiple access schemes, such as time division multiple access (TDMA).

We present a new class of factor analysis methods designed for the joint examination of multiple studies. The objective is to independently identify and estimate 1) factors common across all studies and 2) factors unique to individual studies. We have developed a rapid Expectation Conditional-Maximization algorithm for parameter estimation and established a procedure for selecting the number of common and specific factors. Simulations assess the method's performance, and its application to ovarian cancer gene expression data demonstrates its utility. In both scenarios, we highlight the advantages of joint analysis over standard factor analysis. Ultimately, we aim to offer a valuable tool for accelerating the combination of unsupervised analyses across multiple studies and enhancing the understanding of cross-study signal reproducibility in multivariate data.

Accurately identifying mouse brain microscopy images is a fundamental prerequisite for registering anatomical structures to a reference atlas. While practitioners typically depend on manual image comparison or tools designed for complete images, this study investigates the use of Siamese Networks to locate corresponding 2D reference atlas plates for partial 2D mouse brain images. As a class of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Siamese Networks utilize weight-shared pathways to generate low-dimensional embeddings for image pairs. The matching between a partial brain image and a reference atlas plate is established by calculating the distance between their respective low-dimensional embeddings, derived via contrastive learning. Experimental results demonstrate that Siamese CNNs can precisely identify brain slices using the Allen mouse brain atlas when training and test data originate from the same source, achieving a TOP-1 accuracy of 25% and a TOP-5 accuracy of 100% while processing 29 images in just 7.2 seconds.

Although dimensionality reduction under the $\ell_1$-norm has numerous applications, it remains significantly less understood compared to the Euclidean norm. We introduce two novel oblivious dimensionality reduction methods for the $\ell_1$-norm that offer exponential improvements over previous approaches:

1.  We construct a distribution of random matrices $S \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times n}$, where $r = 2^{\tilde O(d/(\varepsilon \delta))}$. For any matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times d}$, this matrix satisfies, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the condition $\|SAx\|_1 = (1 \pm \varepsilon)\|Ax\|_1$ for all vectors $x$. The matrix $S$ is linear, independent of $A$, and maps $\ell_1$ to $\ell_1$. This result exponentially surpasses the prior best-known construction by Wang and Woodruff (SODA, 2019), which required $r = 2^{2^{\Omega(d)}}$, even when $\varepsilon$ and $\delta$ are constants. Our bound is optimal up to polynomial factors in the exponent, consistent with the known $2^{\sqrt d}$ lower bound for constant $\varepsilon$ and $\delta$.

2.  We propose a distribution of matrices $S \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times n}$, where $k = 2^{O(q^2)}(\varepsilon^{-1} q \log d)^{O(q)}$, enabling the estimation of the entrywise $\ell_1$-norm $\|A\|_1$ for any $q$-mode tensor $A \in (\mathbb{R}^{d})^{\otimes q}$ from $S(A)$. The map $S$ is a tensor product $S^1 \otimes S^2 \otimes \cdots \otimes S^q$, allowing the computation of $S(u_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes u_q)$ for vectors $u_i \in \mathbb{R}^d$ in time $2^{O(q^2)}(\varepsilon^{-1} q \log d)^{O(q)}$. This is substantially faster than the $d^q$ time needed to explicitly form the tensor. Furthermore, this linear map yields a streaming algorithm for independence testing using space $2^{O(q^2)}(\varepsilon^{-1} q \log d)^{O(q)}$, which improves upon the previous doubly exponential space bound of $(\varepsilon^{-1} \log d)^{q^{O(q)}}$ established by Braverman and Ostrovsky (STOC, 2010).

Active inference represents a cutting-edge neuroscience framework that unifies our understanding of brain function and is increasingly applied to AI planning. However, the intricate mathematics involved in developing new models often hinders its adoption in both fields. This paper resolves this barrier by offering a comprehensive mathematical formulation of active inference within discrete time and state spaces, along with the derivation of update equations for novel models. Drawing on the theoretical link between active inference and variational message passing established by John Winn and Christopher M. Bishop in 2005, we utilize this well-defined Bayesian inference method to facilitate the creation of advanced generative models. We demonstrate that employing a fully factorized variational distribution simplifies the expected free energy—thereby clarifying priors over policies so agents can target unambiguous states. Furthermore, we explore future directions involving deep tree searches for sequential policy optimization, grounded in structure learning and belief propagation.

This paper investigates positive solutions to problem $(E)$, defined by the equation $(-\Delta)^{\alpha} u(x)+|u|^{p-1}u(x)=0$ within the region $x\in\Omega\setminus\mathcal{C}$. The problem is subject to the boundary conditions $u(x)=0$ for $x\in\Omega^c$ and a singular condition where $\lim_{x\to\mathcal{C}}u(x)=+\infty$ as $x$ approaches the compact $C^2$ manifold $\mathcal{C}\subset\Omega$. In this context, $\Omega$ is an open bounded $C^2$ domain in $\mathbb{R}^N$, $\mathcal{C}$ is a compact $C^2$ manifold of dimension $N-1$ without boundary, and $p>1$, with the operator $(-\Delta)^{\alpha}$ representing the fractional Laplacian for $\alpha\in(0,1)$. The study establishes the existence of positive solutions for $(E)$ and further examines their uniqueness, asymptotic behavior, and conditions for nonexistence.

We introduce an extension of the three-dimensional Poincaré algebra that incorporates a color symmetry component. This algebraic framework facilitates the formulation of colored Poincaré gravity in three spacetime dimensions and enables the investigation of generalized models for both massive and massless free particles. We detail several such generalized particle models, each distinguished by the specific orbits of the colored Poincaré symmetry they represent. This methodology serves as a foundational step toward describing particles interacting with non-abelian background fields or acts as an initial basis for a worldline formulation of a corresponding quantum field theory.

Achieving high performance in semantic segmentation neural networks typically demands extensive pixel-level annotations, which are particularly costly in the medical field due to the time and expertise required. Active learning addresses this challenge by employing strategies to identify the most informative cases for labeling. This study introduces an Uncertainty Slice Sampling (USS) strategy tailored for annotating 2D image slices within 3D medical volumes, evaluating its effectiveness against alternative methods. Using multi-site CT liver segmentation data, we demonstrate that USS significantly optimizes annotation effort. After five iterations, USS selected only 2,410 slices (4% of the total pool), whereas Uncertainty Volume Sampling (UVS), Random Volume Sampling (RVS), and Random Slice Sampling (RSS) required 8,121 (13%), 8,641 (14%), and 3,730 (6%) slices, respectively. Despite training on the smallest dataset, the USS-based model achieved a mean Dice index of 0.964, a relative volume error of 4.2%, a mean surface distance of 1.35 mm, and a Hausdorff distance of 23.4 mm across 234 test volumes, outperforming models trained with other strategies. Although a model trained on all available data achieved marginally better metrics (Dice: 0.967, volume error: 3.8%, mean surface distance: 1.18 mm, Hausdorff: 22.9 mm), robustness analysis revealed that USS produced the most reliable model. Specifically, based on the 5th percentile of Dice and the 95th percentile of other metrics, USS surpassed the fully trained model in Dice score (0.946 vs. 0.945) and mean surface distance (1.92 mm vs. 2.03 mm).

This research investigates axially symmetric multi-soliton solutions within a complex scalar field theory featuring a sextic potential and minimal coupling to Einstein's gravity. These solutions possess zero angular momentum and are categorized by the number of scalar field nodes, $k_z$, along the symmetry axis. They are understood as gravitationally bound chains of $k_z+1$ boson stars, separated by repulsive scalar forces. Chains composed of an odd number of components display a spiraling relationship between their ADM mass (and Noether charge) and angular frequency, akin to a fundamental boson star, when gravitational coupling is weak. However, at stronger coupling, the inner spiral segment transitions into a merger with the fundamental branch of radially excited spherical boson stars. Conversely, chains with an even number of constituents exhibit a truncated spiral pattern comprising only two or three branches, terminating at a limiting solution characterized by finite ADM mass and Noether charge.

This work investigates $L^p-L^q$ uniform resolvent estimates for two-dimensional Schrödinger operators under scaling-critical magnetic fields, with the Aharonov-Bohm model serving as a primary case study. As an application, we establish localization estimates for the eigenvalues of certain non-self-adjoint zero-order perturbations of the magnetic Hamiltonian.

Enhancing automation within pharmaceutical labs and production sites is vital for ensuring patient access to medicine, yet the sector's unique demands make adapting advanced technologies from other industries difficult. This article reviews relevant strategies for implementation in pharmaceutical development labs, highlighting recent progress such as flexible mobile manipulators for complex tasks. However, integrating heterogeneous devices from multiple vendors into a cohesive automation system remains challenging due to interface diversity. Consequently, this paper examines various standardization approaches and proposes a concept to advance them further. This concept allows a mobile manipulator equipped with a vision system to "learn" device poses and retrieve interface data—such as control/communication protocols and required robot actions—from a universal cloud database via a barcode. To define movements relative to the device, a fiducial marker must be present alongside the barcode as a standard. The detailed elaboration of this concept will be addressed in subsequent research papers.

This paper presents a solution to the waypoint navigation challenge for fixed-wing micro air vehicles (MAVs) within an integrated guidance and control (IGC) framework. Unlike traditional multi-loop architectures, the IGC approach offers a single-step resolution by combining the pure proportional navigation (PPN) guidance law with MAV dynamics. A multivariable static output feedback (SOF) controller is developed for the linear state-space representation defined within this IGC structure. The proposed navigation algorithm accounts for the minimum turn radius constraint inherent to MAVs and assesses the feasibility of reaching designated waypoints. Extensive non-linear simulations conducted on a high-fidelity 150 mm wingspan MAV model illustrate the potential benefits of this algorithm.

We demonstrate that in Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity, a leading non-decaying term in late-time two-point functions arises from a spacetime with Mobius strip topology (a disk with one crosscap). This contribution exhibits a significant interplay with the conventional "plateau," where their sum or cancellation depends on specific topological weighting factors. We align this behavior with Random Matrix Theory (RMT) and the N mod 8 periodicity observed in Sachdev-Kitaev-Ye (SYK) results.

Online social media facilitates open, transparent, and democratized discourse on a wide range of socio-political topics. However, this visibility often attracts manipulation and misinformation, resulting in detrimental consequences. To mitigate such harmful behaviors, platform moderators implement countermeasures to protect against rule violators. Despite this, the general public often finds the connection between published policies and actual enforcement actions opaque. This study investigates violations and subsequent moderation concerning discussions around the 2020 U.S. Presidential Election on Twitter. We aim to quantify the reasons for user suspensions by analyzing Twitter's rules, comparing the activities and characteristics of suspended users (Case) against non-suspended users (Control). Based on a dataset of 240 million election-related tweets from 21 million unique accounts, our findings indicate that suspended users violate Twitter's guidelines at a statistically significant higher rate across all examined categories, including hate speech, offensiveness, spamming, and civic integrity. Furthermore, we qualitatively analyze the specific topics targeted for manipulation through the lens of Twitter's suspension mechanisms.

Accelerating particles to high energies within plasma wakefields is viewed as a highly promising method due to its superior energy efficiency and steep gradients. Although significant strides have been achieved in plasma-based electron acceleration, positron acceleration in such environments remains largely unexplored, with no fully optimized, self-consistent scenario currently established. This capability is nonetheless critical for high-energy physics, particularly for realizing desired electron-positron colliders. Our findings indicate that loading a plasma wakefield with a positron beam can compromise beam quality, necessitating a balance between energy efficiency and beam integrity. For linear plasma wakefields driven by electron beams, we observed that despite the transverse nonlinear focusing forces caused by positron beam loading, the bunch rapidly evolves toward an equilibrium distribution with minimal emittance increase. Particle-in-cell simulations reveal that for normalized emittances at the micrometer scale, the growth of uncorrelated energy spread becomes a significant limiting factor. Our results demonstrate that linear or moderately nonlinear regimes utilizing Gaussian drivers offer an optimal compromise, simultaneously achieving energy-transfer efficiencies above 30% and uncorrelated energy spread below 1%. Conversely, donut-shaped drivers operating in the nonlinear regime are better suited for accelerating high-charge bunches at higher gradients, albeit with a reduced trade-off between efficiency and beam quality.

This study presents a deep learning-driven quantization approach for storing log-likelihood ratios (L-values). By examining the correlation between the average magnitudes of L-values derived from the same quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) symbol, we demonstrate a consistent ranking pattern. Leveraging this insight, we develop a deep autoencoder that simultaneously compresses and individually reconstructs each L-value, employing a weighted loss function to prioritize the accurate recovery of low-magnitude inputs. Results indicate that our method rivals state-of-the-art maximum mutual information quantization techniques, cutting memory requirements by up to half while incurring less than 0.1 dB performance loss with under two effective bits per L-value, or less than 0.04 dB loss with 2.25 effective bits. Furthermore, experiments confirm that our approach functions as a universal compression scheme: a network trained on an LDPC-coded Rayleigh fading scenario can be directly applied to other channel models and coding schemes without additional training, maintaining equivalent performance gains.

We employed rational approximants to analyze missing higher-order contributions in the massless scalar-current quark correlator. Using this approach, we forecast the unknown six-loop coefficient for the imaginary component, which connects to $\Gamma(H\to b \bar b)$, estimating $c_5=-6900\pm 1400$. This prediction renders the perturbative series nearly insensitive to renormalization scale variations and reduces the intrinsic QCD truncation uncertainty to negligible levels. Consequently, this validates the anticipation that further high-order loop calculations for this specific quantity are unnecessary in the near future, since uncertainties in $\Gamma(H\to b \bar b)$ will continue to be primarily driven by Standard Model parameters.

The LHCb experiment conducted a search for the rare decays Bs->mu+mu- and B0->mu+mu- using data from 2011 and 2012 at the Large Hadron Collider. The dataset includes 1.1 fb^-1 of proton-proton collisions at sqrt{s} = 8 TeV and 1.0 fb^-1 at sqrt{s}=7 TeV. An excess of Bs -> mu+ mu- candidates was observed relative to the predicted background, with a probability of 5.3 x 10^-4 for the background to produce such an excess or greater, indicating a signal significance of 3.5 standard deviations. A maximum-likelihood fit yielded a branching fraction of BR(Bs -> mu+ mu-) = (3.2^{+1.5}_{-1.2}) x 10^-9, where the statistical uncertainty accounts for 95% of the total uncertainty. This finding aligns with Standard Model predictions. The number of observed B0 -> mu+ mu- candidates is consistent with the background expectation, resulting in an upper limit of BR(B0 -> mu+ mu-) < 9.4 x 10^-10 at the 95% confidence level.

A candidate triple-strange pentaquark, denoted as $P_{csss}$, is examined via its strong decay mode $P_{csss} \rightarrow \Omega^-J/\psi$. To determine the associated strong coupling constants, two distinct interpolating currents with spin-parity $J^P=\frac{1}{2}^{-}$ are employed. Although these currents are selected for the specific state under study with $J^P=\frac{1}{2}^{-}$, they couple to both positive and negative parity configurations, yielding decay widths for each. When the first current is applied, the calculated widths are $\Gamma(P_{csss} \rightarrow J/\psi \Omega^-)=201.4\pm 76.7~\mathrm{MeV}$ for the negative parity state and $\Gamma(\widetilde{P}_{csss} \rightarrow J/\psi \Omega^-)=316.4\pm 100.3~\mathrm{MeV}$ for the positive parity state. Using the second current, the results are $\Gamma(P_{csss} \rightarrow J/\psi \Omega^-)=252.5\pm 108.6~\mathrm{MeV}$ for negative parity and $\Gamma(\widetilde{P}_{csss} \rightarrow J/\psi \Omega^-)=361.1\pm 88.2~\mathrm{MeV}$ for positive parity. These findings offer valuable insights for future experimental searches of such candidate states and assist in identifying and refining their properties.

We evaluated the biases arising from coherent deflection by the galactic magnetic field (GMF) in prior maximum-likelihood searches for ultra-high-energy cosmic ray (UHECR) sources. By simulating mock event datasets based on assumptions regarding starburst galaxy (SBG) models, coherent GMF deflection, and mixed-mass composition, we performed a maximum-likelihood analysis that ignored the GMF, mirroring previous studies. Our results indicate that the anisotropic fraction ($f_{\rm ani}$) is systematically underestimated. We then identified true parameter sets compatible with the best-fit parameters derived from observations. We found that, aside from a narrow region characterized by a high anisotropic fraction and small angular separation, a broad parameter space remains consistent with the experimental data. Furthermore, we developed a maximum-likelihood method incorporating the GMF model, confirming that this approach yields improved parameter estimates.

$k$NN-based neural machine translation ($k$NN-MT) has demonstrated state-of-the-art performance across numerous machine translation tasks. However, a major limitation of $k$NN-MT is its inefficiency in retrieving the $k$ nearest neighbors from a large datastore, a process that is prohibitively time-consuming. To address this, we introduce **Faster $k$NN-MT**, which employs a hierarchical clustering strategy to approximate distances between queries and datastore entries. This approach decomposes the total distance into two components: the distance from the query to the cluster center, and the distance from the data point to its cluster center. We propose efficient methods to calculate these components, significantly speeding up the process. Extensive experiments on various machine translation benchmarks show that **Faster $k$NN-MT** outperforms Fast $k$NN-MT \citep{meng2021fast} and is only marginally (1.2 times) slower than the standard $k$NN-MT, while maintaining equivalent model performance. This advancement facilitates the deployment of $k$NN-MT models in real-world machine translation services.

This research investigates data-driven attack detection for unknown linear time-invariant (LTI) systems, relying exclusively on input-output behavioral data. Unlike model-based detectors that identify attacks through output prediction errors, we focus on behavior-based detectors. Specifically, we develop a behavior-based chi-squared detector utilizing sequences of inputs, outputs, and their covariance. Covariance estimation is achieved via two approaches: a direct method using sample covariance and an indirect method employing a lower-dimensional generative model derived from data. We demonstrate the consistency of both estimation techniques and establish finite sample error bounds. Furthermore, numerical comparisons reveal a performance tradeoff dependent on the data set size and detection horizon length. Our study shows that neither method is universally superior; instead, two performance regimes exist, where the direct method excels with large data sets relative to the detection horizon, while the indirect method outperforms in scenarios with smaller data sets.

This paper investigates CP violation within photon self-interactions at low energies. These interactions, described by the effective operator $FFF\tilde{F}$ (where $F$ and $\tilde{F}$ represent the electromagnetic and dual field strengths, respectively), have not yet been directly observed experimentally. Potential origins for such phenomena include weakly coupled light scalars with both scalar and pseudoscalar couplings to photons (such as complex Higgs-portal scalars or the relaxion), or new light fermions interacting with photons through dipole operators. We introduce a method to isolate the CP-violating component of photon self-interactions using Superconducting Radio-Frequency cavities and vacuum birefringence experiments. Furthermore, we examine various theoretical and experimental indirect constraints on the new physics scale linked to this effective operator and provide sensitivity projections for the proposed experiments regarding this scale. Finally, we discuss how these bounds impact the CP-violating couplings of new light particles coupled to photons.

This paper establishes Poisson limit laws for open billiard systems featuring boundary holes rather than abstract phase-space holes, a configuration of primary importance for both theoretical analysis and practical applications. The study examines various systems, including Sinai billiards with and without finite horizons, diamond billiards, semi-dispersing billiards, and focusing billiards characterized by slow correlation decay.

State-of-the-art language generation models frequently struggle with problems like repetition, incoherence, and hallucinations. A prevailing theory attributes this fragility to a mismatch between training and generation procedures, known as exposure bias. This paper validates that theory by examining exposure bias through the lens of imitation learning. We demonstrate how exposure bias causes error accumulation, explain why perplexity metrics fail to detect this buildup, and provide empirical evidence that such accumulation degrades generation quality. The source code for reproducing these experiments can be found at https://github.com/kushalarora/quantifying_exposure_bias.

We examine the 3D rotation axes of 77 HI-selected galaxies from the MIGHTEE-HI Early Science survey in relation to cosmic web filaments. For this sample, the alignment between the spin axis and the nearest filament ($\lvert \cos \psi \rvert$) increases with proximity to the filament: galaxies within 5 Mpc show an average alignment of $\langle\lvert \cos \psi \rvert\rangle= 0.66 \pm 0.04$, whereas those between 5 and 10 Mpc average $\langle\lvert \cos \psi \rvert\rangle= 0.37 \pm 0.08$. Furthermore, galaxies with low HI-to-stellar mass ratios ($\log_{10}(M_{\rm HI}/M_{\star}) < 0.11$) exhibit stronger alignment ($\langle\lvert \cos \psi \rvert\rangle= 0.58 \pm 0.04$) compared to those with higher ratios ($\log_{10}(M_{\rm HI}/M_{\star}) > 0.11$), which tend to be misaligned ($\langle\lvert \cos \psi \rvert\rangle= 0.44 \pm 0.04$). Our findings suggest tentative alignment between the spin axes of HI-selected galaxies and filaments (within 10 Mpc), contingent on gas fractions. Specifically, galaxies with higher stellar mass relative to gas mass display stronger alignment. This implies that galaxies with high gas fractions relative to stellar mass may have experienced disrupted alignment due to recent gas-rich mergers, while those without significant recent gas replenishment maintain orientation toward the filament. Additionally, we investigated a predicted spin transition at $M_{\mathrm{HI}}\approx 10^{9.5} M_{\odot}$ based on simulations but found no evidence for it in the current dataset.

Fine-tuning image-text models like CLIP yields state-of-the-art results across numerous benchmarks. Nevertheless, recent studies such as WiseFT (Wortsman et al., 2021) and LP-FT (Kumar et al., 2022) demonstrate that minor variations in the fine-tuning procedure can result in significant performance disparities for both in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) data. This paper presents a straightforward and natural method of emulating contrastive pretraining that consistently surpasses other fine-tuning strategies. Specifically, we treat downstream class labels as text prompts and continue optimizing the contrastive loss between image embeddings and embeddings of descriptive class prompts (contrastive fine-tuning). Our approach consistently beats baselines across 7 distribution shift, 6 transfer learning, and 3 few-shot learning benchmarks. On the WILDS-iWILDCam dataset, our proposed method, FLYP, exceeds the top leaderboard performance by $2.3\%$ ID and $2.7\%$ OOD, achieving the highest reported accuracy. Averaged across 7 OOD datasets (comprising 2 WILDS and 5 ImageNet-related shifts), FLYP delivers $4.2\%$ OOD gains over standard fine-tuning and beats the current state of the art (LP-FT) by over $1\%$ in both ID and OOD settings. Similarly, on 3 few-shot learning benchmarks, our method achieves improvements of up to $4.6\%$ over standard fine-tuning and $4.4\%$ over the state of the art. Collectively, these benchmarks establish contrastive fine-tuning as a simple, intuitive, and state-of-the-art strategy for supervised fine-tuning of image-text models such as CLIP. The code is available at https://github.com/locuslab/FLYP.

To deploy an application within a Kubernetes cluster, a manifest file must be sent to the cluster's control plane. This process is usually executed via the `kubectl` client, which is configured and authorized to interact with the control plane's URL. Applications often depend on numerous Kubernetes resources, including pods, deployments, secrets, services, and volumes. Managing each of these components through individual manifest files demands complex scripting, particularly when many resources are involved. Helm offers a solution to these intricate management challenges by providing both a tool and a framework that bundle the required manifest files. These bundles are deployed using a single install command, which abstracts the underlying interactions with the control plane from the user. Much like application installations managed by Debian's `dpkg`, Helm packages are shared via local and remote repositories, enabling users to easily install, update, delete, or manage concurrent versions.

This research examines the radiation reaction experienced by an accelerating charge within noncommutative spacetime, deriving a corresponding expression. Specifically, the radiation reaction from a nonrelativistic point charge includes a minor noncommutative correction. Furthermore, the Abraham-Lorentz equation for a point charge in such a spacetime continues to exhibit the well-known issues of pre-acceleration and runaway solutions. As an application, we investigate the radiation reaction encountered by a charge undergoing harmonic oscillations within a noncommutative plane.

Generic Event Boundary Detection (GEBD) represents a recently introduced video understanding task designed to identify deeper semantic boundaries of events. By bridging the gap between natural human perception and machine understanding, GEBD offers diverse applications, such as interpretable and semantically accurate video parsing. Although currently in its early stages, existing solvers for GEBD are merely simple adaptations of related video understanding tasks, often overlooking the task's unique characteristics. To address this, we propose a novel framework capable of handling both unsupervised and supervised GEBD using the Temporal Self-similarity Matrix (TSM) as the video representation. Our new Recursive TSM Parsing (RTP) algorithm detects boundaries by leveraging local diagonal patterns within the TSM and is paired with a Boundary Contrastive (BoCo) loss to train the encoder for generating more informative TSMs. This framework achieves state-of-the-art performance with a significant margin on GEBD benchmarks in both unsupervised and supervised settings. Notably, our unsupervised approach surpasses the previous state-of-the-art supervised model, demonstrating its exceptional efficacy.

Although imitation learning presents a promising avenue for robots to acquire general-purpose behaviors, it has historically struggled with scalability due to heavy data supervision needs and fragile generalization. Drawing inspiration from recent progress in multi-task imitation learning, we explore leveraging data from previous tasks to enable robust and data-efficient learning of new tasks. To effectively utilize this prior data, robots must encode knowledge from past experiences and adapt it to novel contexts. Accordingly, we propose a skill-based imitation learning framework that identifies temporally extended sensorimotor skills from historical data and trains a policy for the target task by invoking these acquired skills. We highlight several critical design choices that enhance performance on new tasks, specifically representation learning objectives that yield more predictable skill representations and a retrieval-based data augmentation strategy that broadens the supervision available for policy training. Experiments across various simulated and real-world manipulation domains show that our approach significantly surpasses current imitation learning and offline reinforcement learning methods. Videos and code can be found at https://ut-austin-rpl.github.io/sailor.

High-energy photons can undergo the nonlinear Breit-Wheeler process to produce electron-positron pairs upon colliding with an intense laser pulse. However, the resulting particles exhibit a broadened energy spectrum due to fluctuations in their effective mass throughout the pulse duration. By applying an appropriate chirp to the laser, this energy distribution can be narrowed. We describe a scenario where a high-energy electron beam interacts with a chirped laser to generate a beam of nearly monoenergetic gamma photons. These photons subsequently decay within a second chirped ultraviolet pulse, yielding a quasi-monoenergetic source of high-energy electrons and positrons.

The survey examines case studies covering sales time series forecasting, deep learning methods for non-stationary series with time trend correction, dynamic price and supply optimization via Q-learning, Bitcoin price modeling, the impact of COVID-19 on stock markets, and the application of social network signals in analytics. Additionally, the analysis explores the use of machine learning and Bayesian inference within predictive analytics.

Most text generation systems follow left-to-right (L2R) or right-to-left (R2L) word sequences, mirroring how natural language is typically written. However, our research indicates that this specific writing order is not a strict requirement for generating text. This paper introduces Spiral Language Modeling (SLM), a flexible framework that allows sentence construction to extend beyond traditional L2R and R2L constraints. SLM enables the formation of natural language by initiating generation from any arbitrary token within the final text and expanding outward to the surrounding tokens. By treating the decoding order as an additional optimization objective alongside language model perplexity, SLM enhances both the diversity and quality of generated outputs. Moreover, it allows for control over the text construction process by choosing specific starting tokens. To further boost model robustness, especially in low-resource settings, SLM incorporates generation orderings as an extra form of regularization. Experiments across eight widely studied Neural Machine Translation (NMT) tasks demonstrate that SLM consistently outperforms conventional L2R decoding, achieving up to a 4.7 BLEU point increase.

The BESIII Collaboration has recently identified a resonance, $Y(2040)$, characterized by a mass of $2034\pm13\pm9$ MeV and a width of $234\pm30\pm25$ MeV observed in the $e^+e^-\rightarrow\omega\pi^0$ channel. Furthermore, the BESIII and BABAR Collaborations have secured significantly more precise measurements for the $\rho(1900)$ and $\rho(2150)$ states. This study conducts a comprehensive analysis of the excited $\rho$ resonance mass spectrum using the modified Godfrey-Isgur model and investigates the strong decays of $Y(2040)$, $\rho(1900)$, and $\rho(2150)$ via the $^3P_0$ model. Our findings suggest that $Y(2040)$, $\rho(1900)$, and $\rho(2150)$ correspond to the $\rho(2^3D_1)$, $\rho(3^3S_1)$, and $\rho(4^3S_1)$ states, respectively. Additionally, we predict the mass and strong decay properties of the $\rho(3^3D_1)$ state, which may facilitate its discovery in future experiments.

This study introduces an integer decomposition technique. Initially, an integer is expressed as a polynomial in 2, where all coefficients are restricted to either 0 or 1. Subsequently, if an integer is factored into the product of two such polynomials with degrees exceeding one, equating the coefficients on both sides yields a system of multivariate quadratic equations. Consequently, the problem of integer decomposition is converted into solving this system of quadratic equations. Moreover, the approach further reduces the integer decomposition task to solving a system of linear equations, where the variable count does not surpass the base-2 logarithm of the decomposed number. A key benefit of this method is its directness, eliminating the need for guessing, a feature absent in conventional approaches.

The count of known periodic variables has expanded rapidly in recent times. The Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF), with its extensive field of view and sensitivity to faint objects, provides a distinctive platform for identifying variable stars in the northern hemisphere. Utilizing ZTF Data Release 2 (DR2), we have searched for and categorized variables as faint as r ~ 20.6 mag, classifying 781,602 periodic variables into 11 primary categories using an enhanced classification technique. A comparison with existing catalogs reveals that 621,702 objects (79.5%) represent new discoveries or classifications, comprising approximately 700 Cepheids, 5,000 RR Lyrae stars, 15,000 Delta Scuti variables, 350,000 eclipsing binaries, 100,000 long-period variables, and 150,000 rotational variables. Our method achieves a typical misclassification rate and period accuracy of roughly 2% and 99%, respectively. With 74% of the variables situated at Galactic latitudes |b| < 10°, this extensive sample of Cepheids, RR Lyrae, Delta Scuti stars, and contact (EW-type) eclipsing binaries significantly improves the completeness, spatial coverage, and age resolution available for studying the Galaxy's disk structure and evolution. Notably, the northern warp and the disk's edge at distances of 15–20 kpc are now much better mapped than before. Furthermore, RS Canum Venaticorum and BY Draconis-type rotational variables can be readily distinguished, which will greatly enhance statistical analyses of stellar chromospheric activity.

Certain ill-conditioned algebraic equations pose challenges in deriving accurate roots and coefficients, often requiring multiple-precision floating-point arithmetic. While problems with simple roots are well-conditioned when solved via the eigensolver (provided the associated companion matrix has a small condition number), directly addressing them using Newton or simultaneous iteration methods (collectively termed direct iterative methods) is considered ill-conditioned due to the increasing density of their root distributions. Although the direct iterative method demands a higher number of floating-point mantissa digits compared to the eigenvalue approach, the overall computational expense remains indeterminate. This study focuses on Wilkinson's example and the Chebyshev quadrature problem as representative ill-conditioned cases, presenting numerical evidence that demonstrates the direct iterative method can outperform standard eigensolvers.

Nature exhibits spontaneous mirror symmetry violation during the transition between standard left (or right)-handed spaces and their mirror counterparts (right/left), where particles in these respective domains exhibit distinct lifetimes. Consequently, within a unified field theory of elementary particles, all equations of motion incorporate mass, energy, and momentum as matrices, reflecting the concept that left-handed neutrinos are long-lived while right-handed ones are short-lived. These concepts necessitate moving beyond traditional chiral definitions of matter field structures, acknowledging that Dirac matrices, when presented in the Weyl form, reduce to matrices with internal undisclosure. We propose a theory introducing a new principle: the set-matrix duality as a criterion for matrices. This relationship provides precise mathematical definitions for internally disclosed and undisclosed matrices, enabling the formulation of four additional definitions, three lemmas, and one pair of axioms. This framework implies that no single matrix exists for which an absolutely empty matrix is absent. The resulting sets of matrix elements and matrices of set elements integrate all necessary matrix and set operations to resolve issues within a unified whole.

X-ray reverberation mapping has become a valuable method for investigating accretion processes in active galactic nuclei (AGNs), offering a potent means to study accretion at the scale of the black hole. Typically, observed time lags and relativistic spectral features are analyzed using the lamp-post model framework. Specifically targeting the predictions of relativistic reverberation models, we conducted observations on several of the brightest X-ray Seyfert galaxies using various observing programs. This study presents findings from two extensive campaigns utilizing NuSTAR to observe MCG-5-23-16 and SWIFT J2127.4+5654 within the 3–50 keV energy range; these two sources were among three that initially exhibited signs of a delayed Compton hump. Benefiting from exposure times triple those of previous analyses, we detected no evidence for relativistic reverberation in MCG-5-23-16, with its energy-dependent lags aligning with a log-linear continuum. For SWIFT J2127.4+5654, while a continuum-only model adequately explains the data, the relativistic reverberation model offers a statistically significant improvement in fitting the energy- and frequency-dependent lags, albeit with parameters inconsistent with the time-averaged spectrum. These results contribute to growing evidence that lag data does not conform to a static lamp-post model.

We conducted a photometric survey to discover new cataclysmic variable (CV) stars, specifically targeting potential AR~Scorpii-type binaries. By selecting GAIA sources linked to unidentified X-ray emissions and analyzing light curves from the Zwicky Transient Facility, the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, and Taiwan's Lulin One-meter Telescope, we evaluated eight CV candidates. This effort yielded six new identifications; the remaining two were previously recognized but lacked detailed analysis. We identified two eclipsing systems tied to unidentified XMM-Newton or Swift sources and one promising polar candidate associated with an unidentified ASKA source. Two of the polar candidates reside within the CV period gap, while the other six have orbital periods shorter than this gap. Although no definitive AR~Scorpii-type binary was found, our findings suggest that CV systems exhibiting X-ray emission without frequent outbursts may have been overlooked in prior surveys.

Precise and dependable predictions of emerging dominant SARS-CoV-2 variants allow policymakers and vaccine developers to prepare for future infection surges. Our artificial intelligence models, which integrate biophysics, viral genome genotyping, experimental data, algebraic topology, and deep learning, accurately anticipated the last three waves driven by the Omicron subvariants BA.1, BA.2, and BA.4/BA.5. Leveraging recent experimental findings, we evaluated how every possible mutation in the viral spike protein's receptor-binding domain (RBD) influences SARS-CoV-2 infectivity. This analysis clarifies viral evolutionary strategies, specifically natural selection favoring enhanced infectivity and antibody resistance. We project that BA.2.10.4, BA.2.75, BQ.1.1, and especially the BA.2.75+R346T variant, possess a high likelihood of becoming the next dominant strains to trigger a new surge.

A.Galajinsky recently proposed an N=1 supersymmetric extension of the Euler top and provided insightful observations regarding its properties [arXiv:2111.06083 [hep-th]]. This paper employs a formulation of the Euler top as a system defined on the complex projective plane, which serves as the phase space and functions as a one-dimensional mechanical system. Furthermore, we introduce a supersymmetrization scheme for generic one-dimensional systems with positive Hamiltonians, resulting in a family of a priori integrable N=2k supersymmetric Hamiltonians parameterized by N/2 arbitrary real functions.

Despite recent and ongoing surveys, hot, compact, hydrogen-deficient pre-white dwarfs (pre-WDs) with effective temperatures exceeding 70,000 K and surface gravities between 5.0 and 7.0 remain rare. These objects are thought to arise from either single-star evolution (triggered by late helium-shell or helium-core flashes) or binary evolution (via double white dwarf mergers). Studying them is valuable because their surface elemental abundances reveal the physics underlying thermonuclear flashes and merger events. Spectroscopically, they fall into three categories: PG1159, O(He), and He-sdO. This work presents a spectroscopic analysis of five such stars, which exhibit atmospheric parameters within the ranges Teff = 70,000–80,000 K and log g = 5.2–6.3. Among the three He-sdO stars examined, two possess a relatively high hydrogen mass fraction of 10%, a finding inconsistent with both single-star (helium core flash) and binary (helium white dwarf merger) evolutionary models. The O(He) star JL9 is likely a binary helium white dwarf merger, yet its 6% hydrogen content also conflicts with merger predictions. We identified RL 104 as the coolest member of the PG1159 class at the pre-WD stage, with a temperature of 80,000 K. Its optical spectrum is notable for displaying C IV lines involving Rydberg states with principal quantum numbers up to n = 22. RL 104's low mass (0.48 +0.03/-0.02 Msun) poses a challenge to the standard evolutionary scenario for PG1159 stars, which typically results from a very late helium-shell flash. A similar mass discrepancy arises in merger models involving a close He-sdO and CO white dwarf binary that would predict PG1159-like abundances. Consequently, it is proposed that RL 104 may originate from a very late helium-shell flash in a CO/helium white dwarf formed by the merger of two low-mass helium white dwarfs.

Although numerous studies have employed Machine Learning (ML) techniques to identify Software Vulnerabilities (SVs) within functions and specific code statements, few have utilized these detection results for data-driven SV assessment to evaluate exploitability, impact, and severity. Such metrics are crucial for understanding vulnerabilities and prioritizing remediation. Leveraging extensive data from 1,782 functions across 429 SVs in 200 real-world projects, we explore ML models to automate function-level SV assessment by predicting seven Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) metrics. We specifically examine the utility of vulnerable statements as inputs, given that function-level SVs originate from these statements. Our findings indicate that while vulnerable statements are 5.8 times smaller in size, they demonstrate 7.5% to 114.5% superior assessment performance (measured by Matthews Correlation Coefficient) compared to non-vulnerable statements. Furthermore, incorporating the context of vulnerable statements boosts performance by up to 8.9%, achieving an MCC of 0.64 and an F1-Score of 0.75. In summary, we establish initial yet promising ML-based baselines for function-level SV assessment, opening avenues for future research in this domain.
This paper generalizes Scholze's six functor formalism for diamonds to a broad class of stacky morphisms between v-stacks by employing $\infty$-categorical methods introduced by Liu-Zheng.

Multi-task learning (MTL) effectively enhances the performance of related tasks through knowledge sharing, yet most existing MTL architectures are designed for single-end operation and lack suitability for collaborative intelligence (CI) environments. To address this, we introduce an MTL network integrated with a deep joint source-channel coding (JSCC) framework, enabling deployment within CI scenarios. Initially, we develop a feature fusion-based MTL network (FFMNet) designed for joint object detection and semantic segmentation, which achieves superior performance with reduced parameter counts compared to other MTL approaches. Subsequently, FFMNet is decomposed into two components operating on a mobile device and an edge server, respectively, where intermediate features are transmitted wirelessly from the device to the server. To minimize transmission overhead, a deep JSCC network is engineered; when integrated with FFMNet, the combined model achieves a 512x compression ratio for intermediate features while maintaining performance degradation below 2% on both tasks. Finally, by incorporating noise during training, the FFMNet with JSCC demonstrates robustness across diverse channel conditions and surpasses separate source and channel coding schemes.

This paper introduces high-order (zeroing) barrier functions, an extension of zeroing barrier functions that ensures set forward invariance through the verification of higher-order derivatives. This approach guarantees asymptotic stability of the forward invariant set, offering enhanced robustness against model perturbations. Unlike existing high-order barrier function methods, our formulation does not require the assumption of forward completeness. For controlled dynamical systems, we eliminate the need for a uniform relative degree and present a singularity-free control strategy that produces a locally Lipschitz control signal while ensuring safety. Additionally, the proposed framework addresses "performance-critical" control by guaranteeing that a specific subset of the forward invariant set remains compatible with any existing bounded control law, all while maintaining forward invariance. Finally, we examine a non-trivial case study involving rigid-body attitude dynamics and interconnected cell regions as the safe set.

In this presentation, I outlined how the observed dark matter (DM) relic abundance can be explained within models featuring three interconnected sectors: the DM, the Standard Model (SM), and a light mediator. This framework is examined specifically through the lens of the massive dark photon model, where the DM links to the SM via kinetic mixing between the hypercharge gauge boson and the vector gauge boson of a new $U(1)'$ gauge symmetry. Within these portal models, the DM relic abundance can be generated through no fewer than nine distinct regimes driven by five dynamical mechanisms. Notably, I highlight the sequential freeze-in mechanism, which arises when the dark photon is massive and involves two successive freeze-in processes.

We investigate radiative transfer involving newly proposed feebly-interacting bosons (FIBs)—including axions, axion-like particles (ALPs), dark photons, and similar candidates—by starting from first principles. Our approach simplifies the problem by considering only boson emission, absorption (and decay), while excluding scattering between different radiation modes. Using specified stellar temperature profiles and FIB absorption rates, we derive explicit volume-integral formulas for boson luminosity that span from the free-streaming regime to the strong-trapping limit. In the strong-trapping limit, the system exhibits quasi-thermal emission from a "FIB sphere" consistent with the Stefan-Boltzmann law. These findings improve upon recent expressions and approximations for FIB emission from supernova cores and, specifically for radiatively unstable FIBs, yield explicit formulas for the nonlocal ("ballistic") energy transfer recently observed in horizontal-branch stars.

This study examines how quintessence dark energy influences black hole shadows in the presence of various accretion models. For thin disk accretion, the resulting images consist of dark and bright regions, featuring direct emission, lensing rings, and photon rings. While specific details vary based on emission profiles, direct emission generally dominates the observed brightness, whereas lensing rings contribute minimally and photon rings are negligible. The cosmological horizon significantly impacts these shadows because observers in the outer communication domain are located near it. Regarding spherically symmetric accretion, we analyze both static and infalling matter scenarios. Our findings indicate that the positions of photon spheres remain identical for both cases; however, the specific intensity of the image appears darker for infalling accretion compared to static accretion, a difference attributed to the Doppler effect caused by the inward motion.

This study presents a comparative analysis of deep learning approaches for predicting Mean Opinion Scores (MOS) in synthesized speech, specifically within the Interspeech VoiceMOS challenge. Leveraging data from the challenge's main track, the authors evaluate existing predictors and introduce new models, categorizing them into two groups: NISQA-based architectures and techniques utilizing fine-tuned self-supervised learning (SSL) models, specifically wav2vec2_base. The results indicate that a streamlined version of NISQA, containing 40% fewer parameters, matches the performance of the original architecture across both utterance-level and system-level metrics. Furthermore, pre-training NISQA on its dedicated corpus enhances utterance-level scores but yields no gains at the system level. In terms of overall capability, NISQA-based models perform comparably to three challenge baselines: LDNet, MOSANet, and one other. In contrast, fine-tuning wav2vec2_base demonstrates superior results compared to NISQA-based approaches. The research also highlights a domain mismatch between natural and synthetic speech, revealing that SSL model performance consistently declines when fine-tuned on natural speech data. Additionally, the study finds that incorporating CNN features alongside the SSL model fails to improve baseline performance, and finally, it establishes that the type of synthesis system significantly influences the predictions made by non-SSL models.

A system in stable equilibrium possesses a potential energy at its minimum value. This characteristic is utilized to develop a formula for assessing the stability of floating bodies. It has been determined that a floating body achieves stable equilibrium when its center of gravity is positioned at the lowest possible height relative to its associated center of buoyancy.

This study examines a prey-predator model incorporating additional food, characterized by a Holling type IV functional response and driven by a combination of continuous white noise and discontinuous Lévy noise. We establish the existence and uniqueness of global positive solutions for this system. By treating the quality and quantity of supplementary food as control variables, we formulate a time-optimal control problem and derive the conditions required for the existence of an optimal control. Utilizing the arrow condition within the sufficient stochastic maximum principle, we determine the optimal quality and quantity of additional food. Finally, numerical examples are presented to validate these theoretical results, highlighting their relevance to biological conservation and pest management.

**Objective:** This study evaluates the impact of (1) the statical admissibility of the computed solution and (2) the capacity of the solution to capture singular behavior on the accuracy, local, and global effectivity of recovery-based error estimators applied to enriched finite element methods, such as the extended finite element method (XFEM).

**Design/Methodology:** The performance of two recovery strategies is analyzed. The first is the recently introduced superconvergent patch recovery procedure with equilibration and enrichment (SPR-CX). The second is the extended moving least squares recovery (XMLS), which enriches the solution basis but does not enforce equilibrium constraints. Both methods utilize an enriched polynomial basis incorporating singular terms to more accurately describe the singular characteristics of the solution.

**Findings:** Numerical comparisons of convergence rates and effectivity indices between the enriched techniques and standard non-enriched approaches demonstrate the necessity of employing extended recovery methods within Zienkiewicz-Zhu type error estimators for this problem class. Furthermore, the results highlight substantial improvements in effectivity when using statically admissible recovered solutions.

**Originality/Value:** This research establishes that both extended recovery procedures and the enforcement of statical admissibility are essential for accurately assessing the quality of approximations in enriched finite element methods.

Recently, subspace diagonalization has emerged as a promising strategy for determining the ground and certain excited states of molecular Hamiltonians by classically diagonalizing small matrices, with elements efficiently generated by a quantum computer. The newly introduced Variational Quantum Phase Estimation (VQPE) algorithm utilizes a basis of real time-evolved states, allowing energy eigenvalues to be extracted directly from the unitary matrix $U = \exp(-iHt)$, which is computable at a cost linear to the number of states. This paper presents a circuit-based implementation of VQPE for arbitrary molecular systems, evaluating its performance and resource requirements for $H_2$, $H_3^+$, and $H_6$. Additionally, we propose employing Variational Fast Forwarding (VFF) to reduce the quantum circuit depth required for time evolution within VQPE. We demonstrate that this approximation yields a robust basis for Hamiltonian diagonalization even when fidelity to the exact time-evolved states is low. In scenarios with high fidelity, we show that the approximate unitary $U$ can be diagonalized directly, maintaining the linear cost characteristic of exact VQPE.

Leveraging the core-periphery architecture and pronounced homophilic traits inherent in online social networks, we have engineered algorithms that are both more rapid and precise for forecasting user interests. In contemporary social networks, a small cohort of influential users forms the core with publicly accessible interest profiles, while the vast majority of peripheral users connect to these leaders due to shared interests. Our strategy involves inferring the interests of peripheral nodes by analyzing the interests of their influential neighbors. To achieve this, we require a formal framework elucidating how shared interests drive network formation; consequently, we introduce the Nearest Neighbor Influence Model (NNIM), a stochastic interest formation model inspired by the Hegselmann-Krause opinion dynamics, designed to illustrate how homophily constructs network structures. Utilizing NNIM, we devise an efficient method for predicting peripheral user interests. Technically, we employ Variational Expectation-Maximization to optimize the instantaneous likelihood function via a mean-field approximation of NNIM. We demonstrate that our algorithm converges rapidly and scales effectively to networks containing millions of nodes. Experimental evaluations on standard benchmarks reveal that our approach executes up to two orders of magnitude faster than existing top-performing node embedding techniques while maintaining comparable accuracy.

There exists a face of a convex polyhedron P and a partition L of P into geodesic convex polygons such that no connected "edge" unfolding of P avoids self-intersections, where the unfolding's spanning tree is a subset of the edge skeleton of L.

Social scientists and computer scientists alike are keenly interested in how social contexts shape dialogue behavior, particularly regarding the development of methods to infer these contexts. This paper investigates the interplay of power, gender, and dialogue within organizational settings. To facilitate this research, we developed the Gender Identified Enron Corpus, a resource that semi-automatically attributes gender to approximately 23,000 individuals responsible for roughly 97,000 emails. This freely accessible dataset is significantly larger than any previously existing gender-identified email corpus. Utilizing this resource, we conducted a large-scale analysis of how gender and power dynamics interact. We posit that power manifestation in dialogue is influenced not only by an individual's own gender but also by the "gender environment," defined as the gender composition of their conversation partners. Our study specifically examines power dynamics in two structural dimensions: superficial patterns that ignore textual content, such as contribution frequency and reply rates, and deeper structures embedded within the text, such as the issuance and response to requests. Our findings indicate that both personal gender and the gender environment shape how power is expressed in dialogue, revealing distinct underlying patterns. Furthermore, we demonstrate the practical application of gender data in automatically predicting the direction of power between participants in email exchanges.

This paper introduces fully distributed multi-group multicast precoding frameworks tailored for cell-free massive MIMO systems that require minimal training overhead. Our primary objective is to minimize the aggregate of the maximum mean squared errors (MSEs) across all multicast groups; to streamline computation and signaling, this goal is approximated as a weighted sum MSE minimization problem. To achieve joint, fully distributed design of network-wide precoders at base stations (BSs) and combiners at user equipments (UEs), we employ an iterative bi-directional training protocol utilizing UE-specific or group-specific precoded uplink pilots alongside group-specific precoded downlink pilots. Crucially, we propose a novel group-specific uplink training resource that completely removes the necessity for backhaul signaling during channel state information (CSI) exchange. Precoders are optimized locally at each BS using either best-response or gradient-based update mechanisms, and we analyze the convergence of both methods relative to a centralized implementation with perfect CSI. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed distributed approaches significantly outperform conventional cell-free massive MIMO precoding schemes that depend exclusively on local CSI.

We present a novel proof establishing homological stability for mapping class groups of surfaces with respect to genus, achieving the currently best-known isomorphism range. This approach applies the frameworks of Randal-Williams-Wahl and Krannich to disk stabilization within the category of bidecorated surfaces, utilizing Euler characteristic rather than genus as the grading parameter. Although the monoidal category of bidecorated surfaces lacks a braiding—setting it apart from prior contexts for homological stability—we demonstrate that it possesses a suitable Yang-Baxter element, providing the necessary structure for these stability arguments.

This paper investigates how (dual) relative CS-Rickart properties are transferred between abelian categories through functors, specifically examining both fully faithful functors and adjoint pairs. Furthermore, we present multiple applications within Grothendieck categories, with a particular focus on (graded) module and comodule categories.

Most globular clusters (GCs) exhibit signs of multiple stellar populations, indicating several separate star-formation events. The significant number of second-generation (2P) stars implies that a substantial mass of 2P gas must have gathered in the cluster core to facilitate their creation, necessitating that the first-generation (1P) stars were embedded within this gas just before subsequent populations formed. This study investigates the evolution of binaries within the ambient 2P gaseous environments of multi-population GCs, with a primary focus on black hole binaries. We trace their development from wide binaries to short orbital periods via gas interactions, followed by gravitational-wave (GW) driven inspiral and merger. We demonstrate that this novel gas-mediated GW-merger channel could significantly contribute to the generation of GW sources. By examining various assumptions and initial conditions, we calculated the gas-induced changes in the binary population and the resulting merger rates from gas-catalyzed GW inspirals. Under plausible conditions, we estimate an observable GW merger rate for aLIGO of up to a few tens of $\rm{Gpc^{-3} yr^{-1}}$, with a total model range of $0.08-25.51 \ \rm{Gpc^{-3} yr^{-1}}$. Ultimately, our findings suggest that gas interactions critically influence early-stage GC conditions and binary properties, potentially requiring a substantial revision of current GC evolution models.

N-polar AlN epilayers were successfully fabricated on the N-face of single-crystal bulk AlN substrates using plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy (PA-MBE). The removal of native surface oxides and impurities from the N-polar substrate, which facilitated successful homoepitaxy, was achieved through a combination of high-temperature in situ thermal deoxidation and Al-assisted thermal desorption. Epitaxial layers grown on these in situ cleaned substrates under a sufficiently high Al droplet regime displayed smooth surface morphologies characterized by clean and wide atomic steps. KOH etching confirmed the N-polarity of these homoepitaxial films. Secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) revealed that Si and H impurity concentrations fell below detection limits, while O and C impurity levels were approximately 8×10¹⁷ atoms/cm³ and 2×10¹⁷ atoms/cm³, respectively. Although structural defect densities remained low, these defects notably manifested as inversion domains of varying dimensionalities.

We demonstrate that orthogonal separable coordinates on any (pseudo-)Riemannian manifold inherently form a projective variety, which admits an action by the isometry group. This insight motivates a novel algebraic geometric method for classifying such coordinates by analyzing the properties of this variety. Furthermore, we present a case where this method uncovers unforeseen structural details within the established classification and outline several problems that naturally emerge from this framework.

The success of self-attention-based architectures like the Vision Transformer (ViT) in surpassing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) across visual tasks has extended the Transformer paradigm from language processing to computer vision. This approach has recently been adapted for audio, with the Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST) achieving state-of-the-art performance on classification benchmarks. However, pure Transformer models typically demand extensive training data compared to CNNs, and the AST's efficacy depends on supervised pretraining that necessitates vast labeled datasets and intricate training procedures, thereby restricting its practical application. This paper addresses audio and speech classification by aiming to diminish AST's reliance on large labeled datasets through self-supervised learning utilizing unlabeled data. We introduce a method to pretrain AST using joint discriminative and generative masked spectrogram patch modeling (MSPM) on unlabeled audio from AudioSet and Librispeech. Our models are evaluated on diverse tasks, including audio event classification, keyword spotting, emotion recognition, and speaker identification. The proposed self-supervised framework substantially enhances AST performance across all tasks, yielding an average improvement of 60.9% and achieving results comparable to or superior to those of supervised pretraining. To our knowledge, this represents the inaugural patch-based self-supervised learning framework for the audio and speech domains and the first such framework specifically designed for AST.

A Cauchy matrix method is introduced to address the SU(2) self-dual Yang--Mills equation. This approach constructs the equation within Yang's framework by utilizing a Sylvester matrix equation paired with specific dispersion relations for infinite coordinates. Subsequently, by applying additional constraints to the complex independent variables, a wide range of explicit solutions are derived.

Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in utilizing natural language to execute intricate tasks. This study investigates whether we can capitalize on this acquired capability to identify and elucidate patterns within data. Specifically, we introduce interpretable autoprompting (iPrompt), an algorithm designed to produce natural-language explanations of data given a pre-trained LLM and sample examples. The iPrompt methodology iteratively cycles between having an LLM generate explanations and reranking them according to their effectiveness as prompts. Evaluations across diverse datasets, ranging from synthetic mathematics to natural-language comprehension, indicate that iPrompt successfully uncovers ground-truth dataset descriptions, yielding significant insights. Furthermore, the prompts generated by iPrompt are both highly effective for generalization and interpretable by humans; on real-world sentiment classification tasks, they perform on par with or surpass human-crafted prompts for GPT-3. Additionally, experiments involving an fMRI dataset highlight the method's potential to facilitate scientific discovery. All associated code and data are publicly available on Github.

By applying the method of moving frames, we investigate the algebra of differential invariants for surfaces within three-dimensional affine geometry. We demonstrate that for elliptic, hyperbolic, and parabolic points, the algebra is generically generated by a single invariant, provided it is non-trivial.

This work establishes a higher-dimensional Chevalley restriction theorem for orthogonal groups, addressing a conjecture by Chen and Ng\^{o} regarding reductive groups. In the case where the characteristic $p>2$, we additionally demonstrate a weaker result. Within characteristic $0$, the theorem ensures that the categorical quotient of a commuting scheme under the diagonal adjoint action of the group is both normal and reduced. Furthermore, we apply these findings to derive several trace identities and establish a specific multiplicative property of the Pfaffian over any commutative algebra.

The progression of information within intricate networks is pivotal to numerous biological processes and social occurrences. Yet, a comprehensive framework to describe this evolution remains missing, leaving many mechanisms obscure. A central, paradoxical issue involves the simultaneous presence of local stochasticity—where information distorts randomly during pairwise transmission—and global order, characterized by predictable non-random patterns across the network. This study formalizes information evolution to resolve this duality. By integrating network dynamics with information theory, we reveal that a specific quantity of data, governed by the network's selectivity toward input, often endures despite random distortion. Conversely, other information inevitably degrades or vanishes, with the rate of this loss dictated by the diversity of selective mechanisms within the network. These principles hold true regardless of noise, though noise amplifies their effects.
