We validate the universality of these findings by examining the development of neural tuning in the primary visual and medial temporal cortices of animal brains, as well as the rise of extreme viewpoints in social networks.

Traditional federated learning involves clients transmitting local model updates based on private data to a central server for aggregation. However, this approach becomes computationally prohibitive when resource-limited clients attempt to train large-scale models by sharing the entire architecture. Split learning offers a viable alternative in such scenarios by partitioning the model, storing and training only a small segment on clients while keeping the bulk of the model on the server. Despite this efficiency, the model splitting inherent in split learning incurs substantial communication overhead. This paper tackles that challenge by introducing a novel clustering technique paired with a gradient correction mechanism to compress the extra communication required. Comprehensive experiments on image and text datasets demonstrate that the proposed method reduces communication costs by up to 490 times with negligible accuracy loss, establishing an optimal balance between performance and communication efficiency.

The object P/2019 LD2 (ATLAS), co-orbital with Gateway Centaur and Jupiter, represents the inaugural chance to witness the migration of a Solar System small body from a Centaur orbit to a Jupiter Family Comet (JFC) over the next four decades (Kareta et al., 2020; Hsieh et al. 2020). Located in the Gateway transition region, beyond the zone where water ice can drive cometary activity, coma production remains as obscure here as it does in other Centaurs. This study presents simultaneous multi-wavelength observations of LD2 from July 2–4, 2020, utilizing Gemini-North visible imaging, NASA IRTF near-infrared spectroscopy, and ARO SMT millimeter-wavelength spectroscopy. Precovery DECam images constrain the nucleus's effective radius to ≤1.2 km, and archival Catalina Sky Survey data reveal no significant outbursts. LD2's coma exhibits color indices of g'-r' = 0.70 ± 0.07 and r'-i' = 0.26 ± 0.07, a dust production rate of approximately 10–20 kg/s, and an outflow velocity ranging from ~0.6 to 3.3 m/s. No CO was detected on July 2–3, 2020, establishing a 3-sigma upper limit of Q(CO) < 4.4 × 10^27 mol/s (<200 kg/s). Near-infrared spectra indicate water ice at the 1–10% level, contingent on grain size. Spatial profiles and archival records align with sustained activity, supporting the hypothesis that LD2 is a representative small Centaur destined to become a typical JFC, thereby underscoring its importance for understanding the transition between these populations. The paper concludes by outlining potential strategies for a community-wide, long-baseline monitoring initiative.

We present and experimentally validate a {\it quantum-inspired} protocol for quantifying the similarity between two spatial shapes within separate optical beams without requiring measurements of amplitude and phase for each individual beam. Instead, the desired information is obtained by measuring the degree of polarization of the combined beam, a significantly more practical experimental approach. This method relies on non-separable optical beams, characterized by the fact that their degrees of freedom—specifically polarization and spatial shape in this context—cannot be described independently.

Session-based Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are increasingly popular for recommendation tasks because they effectively capture the high autocorrelation of recent user behavior and the sequential order of interactions. However, most current session-based RNN systems focus exclusively on short-term interactions within a single session, ignoring long-term data spanning multiple sessions. Although traditional Collaborative Filtering (CF) methods have advanced research on long-term dependencies that could significantly benefit deep learning models, this potential remains largely untapped in session-based contexts. To address this, we introduce ASARS, a novel framework that integrates temporal dynamics from CF into session-based RNNs using a parallel attentional network to treat temporal information as scalable weights. First, we conducted extensive data analysis to demonstrate the distribution and significance of temporal interactions both within and across sessions. Subsequently, the ASARS framework proposes two new models: (1) an inter-session temporal dynamic model that captures long-term user interactions by integrating time variations into session RNNs and modeling user preference drift; and (2) a novel triangle parallel attention network that enhances the original RNN by incorporating time information. This triangle network is specifically designed to enable efficient data augmentation in sequence-to-scalar RNN architectures, allowing for rapid training. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets from diverse domains confirm the effectiveness and substantial improvements of ASARS in personalized recommendation.

Recent years have seen growing interest in halide perovskites for spintronics, driven by their highly adjustable spin-orbit fields and complex interactions with lattice symmetry. Although the spin lifetime—a critical metric for both spintronics and spin-based quantum information technologies—has been widely measured experimentally in these materials, it has not yet been evaluated using first-principles calculations. In this work, we utilize a recently developed ab initio density-matrix dynamics framework to calculate the spin relaxation time ($T_1$) and ensemble spin dephasing time ($T_2^*$) in the model system CsPbBr$_3$. Our approach incorporates self-consistent spin-orbit coupling and quantum descriptions of electron scattering. Furthermore, we derive the Landé g-factor from first principles and integrate it into our dynamics to accurately model spin dephasing under external magnetic fields. These computations predict intrinsic spin lifetimes as an upper limit for experimental values, identify the primary spin relaxation mechanisms, and analyze dependencies on temperature, external fields, carrier density, and impurities. Notably, we determine that the Fröhlich interaction, which governs carrier relaxation, has a negligible impact on spin relaxation, aligning with its spin-conserving character. Ultimately, this theoretical methodology could inform new strategies for optimizing spin and carrier transport for applications in spintronics and quantum information.

This study introduces a technique for addressing multivariate regression and classification tasks through piecewise linear predictors defined over a polyhedral partition of the feature space. The proposed algorithm, termed PARC (Piecewise Affine Regression and Classification), operates by alternating between two main phases: (i) solving ridge regression for numeric outputs, softmax regression for categorical outputs, and either softmax regression or cluster centroid calculation for piecewise linear separation, and (ii) reassigning training data points to clusters based on a criterion that harmonizes prediction accuracy with piecewise-linear separability. We demonstrate that PARC functions as a block-coordinate descent method that optimizes a specifically designed objective function, guaranteeing convergence to a local minimum within a finite number of iterations. Extensive numerical evaluations on both synthetic and real-world datasets confirm the algorithm's accuracy, highlighting its value as an extension to linear regression and classification, especially when the predictor serves as a component within an optimization model. A Python implementation of this algorithm can be accessed at http://cse.lab.imtlucca.it/~bemporad/parc.

Recent progress has allowed a single neural network to function as an implicit scene representation, defining a mapping between spatial coordinates and scene attributes. This paper advances this field by enabling the continual learning of such representations directly from sequential data, a method we term Continual Neural Mapping. Our proposed framework connects the domain of batch-trained implicit neural representations with the streaming data prevalent in robotics and computer vision. To address this, we introduce an experience replay strategy applied to a key continual neural mapping task: approximating a continuous signed distance function (SDF) from sequential depth images to represent scene geometry. We demonstrate, for the first time, that a single network can continuously model scene geometry over time without suffering from catastrophic forgetting, while maintaining a favorable balance between accuracy and efficiency.

Symmetric mass generation refers to a mechanism that induces a mass gap in fermions while maintaining a chiral symmetry that is necessarily non-anomalous. This paper outlines how such generation for continuous symmetries can be realized through gauge dynamics in both two and four dimensions. The discussion involves various strong coupling phenomena, including established characteristics of supersymmetric gauge theories, particularly s-confinement, as well as hypothesized properties of non-supersymmetric chiral gauge theories.

Achieving high average laser powers often relies on directly cooling the slab faces with a fluid flowing through both the pump and main laser beams. Typically, this flow is kept at low Reynolds numbers to avoid turbulence, which can compromise wavefront quality. We demonstrate that cooling the fluid to its thermo-optical null point—near the water/ice transition for water—can counteract the optical effects of hydrodynamic instabilities by optically bleaching temperature variations within the flow. This phenomenon, termed "index-leveling," enables a highly efficient forced-flow cooling regime characterized by weak turbulence, a development poised to significantly enhance the kilowatt-level capabilities of future high-power lasers.

This study aims to make active learning more clinically relevant. In medical practice, diseases present differently across various patient groups. While current frameworks rely on mathematical constructs to engineer uncertainty or diversity-based methods for sample selection, these approaches are not naturally intuitive for medical professionals, leading to limited adoption in clinical settings. To address this, we propose a framework that integrates clinical insights into the active learning sample selection process, compatible with existing algorithms. Our medically interpretable approach captures the diverse manifestations of disease in patients to enhance the generalization performance of OCT classification. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that incorporating patient insights into this framework achieves performance that matches or exceeds five common paradigms across two architectures, even with datasets featuring imbalanced patient distributions. Furthermore, the framework aligns with current medical practices, making it accessible for use by healthcare providers.

Visible light communication (VLC) represents a promising Optical Wireless Communication (OWC) approach, proven to offer secure, line-of-sight (LoS), and short-range connectivity for vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) and vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) interactions. Recent proposals leverage V2I links to enhance the reliability of automated driving systems. Accordingly, we introduce a VLC-based V2I framework designed to boost communication redundancy for autonomous valet parking (AVP) applications by utilizing VLC's jam-free and location-specific attributes. This paper presents a novel architecture facilitating real-time online map updates within indoor parking garages, enabling vehicle onboard data transmission and location-driven map dissemination via bidirectional VLC. The proposed system achieves error-free LoS transmissions using Direct Current Biased Optical OFDM (DCO-OFDM) over distances up to 33 meters, supporting the sharing of vehicle CAN Bus data, infrastructure camera video, and LIDAR point cloud data inside indoor parking facilities.

This paper investigates the Daugavet property, diameter two properties (D2Ps), and diametral D2Ps within Orlicz-Lorentz spaces utilizing the Luxemburg norm. We first provide a complete characterization of the Radon-Nikodým property for these spaces by examining all finite real-valued Orlicz functions, a result achieved by calculating the fundamental functions of their associated K\"othe dual spaces, which are defined via extended real-valued Orlicz functions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that when an Orlicz function fails to meet the requisite $\Delta_2$-condition, both the Orlicz-Lorentz space and its order-continuous subspace exhibit the strong diameter two property. Consequently, provided the Orlicz function is an N-function at infinity, this same condition characterizes the diameter two properties of Orlicz-Lorentz spaces as well as the octahedral nature of their K\"othe dual spaces. Additionally, Orlicz-Lorentz function spaces possessing the Daugavet property and diametral D2Ps are isometrically isomorphic to $L_1$ when the weight function is regular. During this analysis, we note that every locally uniformly nonsquare point is not a $\Delta$-point, thereby identifying a new class of real Banach spaces devoid of $\Delta$-points. Finally, as a further application, we establish that for Orlicz-Lorentz spaces equipped with the Luxemburg norm and defined by an N-function at infinity, their K\"othe dual spaces lack the local diameter two property, and consequently, they also do not possess other diameter two properties, diametral D2Ps, or the Daugavet property.

Given a system of coupled oscillators on an unknown graph and its trajectory over a specific timeframe, can we forecast eventual synchronization? Even with a known graph structure, this remains a critical but generally analytically unsolvable problem. This study adopts an alternative strategy by framing synchronization prediction as a classification task, grounded in the premise that systems either synchronize or converge to non-synchronizing limit cycles. By relying solely on fundamental graph statistics like edge density and diameter, the proposed method achieves perfect accuracy when there are substantial topological differences between synchronizing and non-synchronizing cases. However, when these statistics fail to clearly separate the two classes—such as when graphs originate from the same random model—incorporating a few iterations of initial dynamics alongside graph statistics significantly boosts accuracy, surpassing classical oscillator theory. More notably, in nearly all such scenarios, training algorithms using only initial dynamics, without basic graph statistics, yields accuracy comparable to the combined approach. The method is validated across three models of continuous and discrete coupled oscillators: the Kuramoto model, Firefly Cellular Automata, and the Greenberg-Hastings model. Finally, an "ensemble prediction" algorithm is introduced, which scales the approach to large graphs by leveraging dynamics observed from multiple random subgraphs.

Although recent methods have introduced continuous relaxations to learn Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) via backpropagation as an alternative to combinatorial optimization, fully discrete backpropagation techniques offer another viable path. This paper investigates that avenue by introducing DAG-DB, a framework designed for learning DAGs through Discrete Backpropagation. Building upon the architecture of Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation (I-MLE), DAG-DB employs a probabilistic strategy that samples binary adjacency matrices from an implicit distribution. The framework learns the distribution's parameters based on the loss generated by each sample and demonstrates competitive performance when utilizing either I-MLE or Straight-Through Estimation as fully discrete backpropagation methods.

This study presents Guardian Angel, an Android application designed to help visually impaired individuals navigate complex traffic environments safely. Leveraging a pretrained YOLO model for object detection, alongside distance and direction estimation capabilities, the system alerts users to potential hazards from surrounding vehicles without requiring costly specialized hardware. Experimental results involving eight subjects demonstrate that, at a 99% confidence level, user satisfaction scores during pedestrian crossing tasks with the app significantly outperformed those without it. Although the system did not yield a statistically significant reduction in average road-crossing time, it did facilitate shorter crossings on average. The application is now available for free on the Google Play Store.

This Letter provides compelling reasons to fundamentally revise negative mass cosmology (NMC), a model proposed as a straightforward alternative to dark energy and dark matter within General Relativity. We demonstrate that numerous physical predictions of this framework necessitate fine-tuning to align with existing cosmological data, thereby obscuring the model's original motivation by introducing ad hoc, unknown variables. Consequently, we conclude that a more rigorous theoretical approach is essential for rendering NMC a viable cosmological model.

For a cancellative semigroup $S$ and a field $F$, it is established that the semigroup algebra $FS$ is centrally essential if and only if the group of fractions $G_S$ of $S$ exists and the group algebra $FG_S$ of $G_S$ is centrally essential. Furthermore, the semigroup algebra of a cancellative semigroup is centrally essential if and only if it possesses a classical right ring of fractions that is itself a centrally essential ring. Additionally, non-commutative centrally essential semigroup algebras over fields of zero characteristic do exist, a result that stands in contrast to the established fact that centrally essential group algebras over such fields must be commutative.

Man-made communication signals are generally modeled as continuous-time (CT) wide-sense cyclostationary (WSCS) processes. Since modern processing is digital, it functions on sampled versions of these CT signals. When a CT WSCS process is sampled, the statistical properties of the resulting discrete-time (DT) process rely on the relationship between the sampling interval and the period of the CT process's statistics. If these two parameters share a common integer factor, the DT process remains WSCS, a condition known as synchronous sampling. Conversely, when this alignment does not occur, termed asynchronous sampling, the DT process becomes wide-sense almost cyclostationary (WSACS). This paper investigates the fundamental tradeoff of source coding for sampled CT WSCS processes, specifically the rate-distortion function (RDF). While RDF characterization for synchronous sampling is straightforward using classic information-theoretic tools based on ergodicity and the law of large numbers, asynchronous sampling results in a process that lacks information stability. Consequently, standard information-theoretic tools are inapplicable for RDF analysis in this scenario, presenting a significant challenge. By employing the information spectrum framework, we demonstrate that the RDF for asynchronous sampling in the low distortion regime can be represented as the limit superior of a sequence of RDFs, where each term corresponds to the RDF of a synchronously sampled WSCS process (though the limit itself may not exist). This characterization provides new insights into the interplay between sampling synchronization and RDF. For instance, we show that unlike stationary processes, even minor variations in the sampling rate or time offset can substantially impact the RDF of sampled CT WSCS processes.

Determining nucleation rates from molecular dynamics trajectories is challenging due to slow time scales and finite size effects. This study demonstrates that precise nucleation rates can be derived broadly by utilizing the free energy barrier, Transition State Theory (TST), and a straightforward dynamical correction for diffusive recrossing. Within this framework, the time scale issue is resolved through enhanced sampling techniques, specifically metadynamics, while finite size effects are naturally mitigated by reconstructing the free energy surface from a suitable ensemble. This approach avoids the approximations inherent in classical nucleation theory. The method's accuracy is validated by computing macroscopic droplet nucleation rates from argon vapor across sixteen orders of magnitude, achieving excellent agreement with existing literature using simulations of very small systems containing only 512 atoms.

Boolean programs featuring multiple recursive threads can be modeled as pushdown automata equipped with multiple stacks. While this model is Turing complete, analysis often focuses on restricted subclasses that retain useful behavioral properties. This paper introduces a novel class of bounded under-approximations for multi-pushdown systems, which encompasses the majority of existing approaches. We present an efficient algorithm to solve the under-approximate reachability problem, leveraging optimized fix-point computations. This algorithm has been implemented in the tool BHIM, whose effectiveness is demonstrated through a suite of generated benchmarks and performance evaluations. Additionally, BHIM addresses the binary reachability problem for standard pushdown automata. To highlight the approach's versatility, we further extend the algorithm to the timed domain, delivering the first implementation capable of handling timed multi-pushdown automata with closed guards.

This paper investigates a random geometric graph (RGG) $G$ with $n$ nodes and an adjacency distance $r_n$ situated just below the Hamiltonicity threshold. We aim to construct Hamiltonian cycles by incorporating auxiliary edges, termed bridges, which are not part of $G$. Our primary objective is to determine the required quantity of these bridges and the maximum bridge length necessary for cycle construction. Our main result demonstrates that, with high probability (converging to one as $n \rightarrow \infty$), a Hamiltonian cycle can be formed where the maximum bridge length is a constant multiple of $r_n$, while the fraction of bridge edges remains arbitrarily small. This outcome is achieved through a method combining backbone construction with iterative cycle merging.

Most IoT devices, including smartwatches, smart plugs, and HVAC controllers, rely on hardware with limited specifications—such as low memory, clock speed, and processing power—that cannot support large, high-quality machine learning models. Despite these constraints, manufacturers offer attractive features by adhering to the traditional paradigm of collecting data (images, audio, sensor readings, etc.) and transmitting it to cloud-based ML platforms. However, this online approach has long suffered from issues like compromised data streams, latency-induced non-real-time analytics, bandwidth limitations, expensive subscriptions, and growing privacy concerns highlighted by users and GDPR regulations. To address these challenges and enable ultra-fast, accurate AI-based offline analytics on resource-constrained IoT hardware, this paper introduces an end-to-end, multi-component model optimization sequence and makes its implementation open-source. Developers and researchers can leverage this sequence to optimize memory-intensive and computation-heavy models across multiple dimensions, resulting in compact, low-latency, and low-power models capable of running comfortably on limited hardware. Experimental results demonstrate that our optimization components achieve: (i) a 12.06x compression ratio; (ii) an accuracy improvement of 0.13% to 0.27%; and (iii) unit inference speeds that are orders of magnitude faster at 0.06 ms. Furthermore, this optimization sequence is generic and applicable to any state-of-the-art models used for anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, robotics, voice recognition, and machine vision.

Centering Theory (CT; Grosz et al., 1995) offers a linguistic framework for analyzing discourse structure, positing that local coherence emerges from how successive utterances reference shared entities. This study explores the relationship between Centering Theory and contemporary coreference resolution systems. We propose an operational definition of centering and employ a search-based methodology to systematically evaluate whether neural coreference resolvers comply with CT rules through various discourse metrics. Our information-theoretic analysis indicates a positive correlation between coreference and centering, yet demonstrates that high-performing neural resolvers gain little advantage from explicitly modeling centering concepts. Furthermore, we find that contextualized embeddings encapsulate much of the necessary coherence information, explaining why CT yields minimal improvements for modern neural systems utilizing pretrained representations. Finally, we address coreference factors unmodeled by standard CT, such as world knowledge and recency bias. By formulating an enhanced version of CT that incorporates recency, we show it captures coreference information more effectively than the original formulation.

While earlier research focused on the contact between a rigid punch and an elastic foundation with a power-law variation in Young's modulus, this study investigates the Hertzian and adhesive contact between two elastic bodies that are both inhomogeneous and possess distinct power-law grading exponents. The problem is defined by an integral equation featuring two different power kernels, which is solved using a novel method involving Gegenbauer orthogonal polynomials. This approach yields an infinite system of linear algebraic equations with a unique structure. After evaluating the integral representations of the system's coefficients and analyzing their properties, it is demonstrated that when the exponents are identical, the system admits a simple exact solution applicable to cases where Young's moduli differ but the exponents match. Computationally convenient formulas are derived for the contact zone length, pressure distribution, and normal surface displacements. Furthermore, the impact of discrepancies in the Young's modulus exponents is examined, and a comparative analysis of Hertzian versus adhesive models elucidates how surface energy density influences contact pressure, the size of the contact area, and the deformation profiles of the bodies outside the contact region.

This poster outlines our contributions to Wikimedia's processing pipeline for mathematical formulae. We detail the shift from rendering formulae as coarse-grained PNG images in 2001 to delivering modern, semantically rich, language-independent MathML formulae in 2020. Furthermore, we present our strategies for enhancing the accessibility and discoverability of mathematical knowledge within Wikimedia projects.

This Letter details the ALICE Collaboration's initial measurements of charged-particle multiplicity density ($\rm{d}N_{\rm{ch}}/\rm{d}\eta$) and total multiplicity ($N_{\rm{ch}}^{\rm{tot}}$) in Xe-Xe collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 5.44 TeV. These measurements cover a broad pseudorapidity range ($-3.5 < \eta < 5$) across various collision centralities. When normalized by the number of participating nucleons ($N_{\rm{part}}$), the mid-rapidity density and total multiplicity for central collisions align with trends from prior heavy-ion studies at different energies. Both quantities also rise with increasing $N_{\rm{part}}$, and for the 5% most central events, they match trends observed in Pb-Pb collisions at comparable energies. However, for more central collisions, the scaled multiplicities in Xe-Xe exceed those in Pb-Pb for similar $N_{\rm{part}}$ values. The findings are compared against phenomenological models and theoretical calculations regarding particle production mechanisms; all models describe the data within a 15% margin.

Accurately estimating the prevalence of undocumented SARS-CoV-2 infections is essential for comprehending the full impact of the pandemic. Uncovering these unreported cases holds fundamental significance for shaping public policy and intervention strategies. In this study, we demonstrate a simple yet effective method to calculate the true number of individuals infected with SARS-CoV-2, utilizing raw epidemiological data reported by official health authorities in the largest EU nations and the United States.

This letter presents an experimental demonstration of an efficient method to control coupled nonlinear oscillators by dynamically adjusting their interaction. We observe that introducing time- or state-dependent intermittency into the interaction term predictably modifies the dynamics of the individual oscillators. By selecting whether the interaction is attractive or repulsive, one can either suppress oscillations or stimulate activity. Two parameters, $\Delta$ and $\tau$, which govern the extent of interaction between subsystems, are introduced to serve as a mechanism for accessing the full spectrum of possible behaviors, ranging from fixed points to chaos. For constant system parameters and coupling strength, varying $\Delta$ and $\tau$ provides precise control over the dynamics of the coupled subsystems. We validate these findings experimentally using coupled Chua's circuits and further illustrate their behavior across a range of coupling parameters through detailed numerical simulations.

We have enhanced the tree-level framework from Ref. arXiv:1004.5484 [hep-ph] regarding weak kaon production on nucleons by partially reinstating unitarity. This is accomplished by applying Watson's theorem to the leading vector and axial-vector terms within specific angular momentum and isospin sectors. The study examines the observable implications of this approach.

This study examines quantum coherence within a bipartite system of Alice and Bob in de Sitter space, where they initially share an entangled state across two modes of a free massive scalar field. The analysis demonstrates that space curvature generates both local and correlated coherence, thereby increasing the total coherence of the system. These findings starkly contrast with the Unruh and Hawking effects; under single-mode approximations, those effects fail to produce local coherence while simultaneously destroying correlated coherence, resulting in a net decrease in total bipartite coherence. Notably, quantum coherence exhibits behavior opposite to that of quantum correlation in de Sitter space. Furthermore, the curvature effect of de Sitter space most profoundly impacts quantum coherence in scenarios involving conformal invariance or masslessness. Ultimately, these results highlight the distinct differences between curvature effects in de Sitter space and those associated with the Unruh effect in Rindler spacetime or the Hawking effect in black hole spacetime regarding quantum coherence.

Metal-insulator transitions (MIT) under non-adiabatic conditions often progress through high-energy intermediate states that are challenging to observe or manipulate using static techniques. By utilizing ultrafast electron diffraction to track the out-of-equilibrium structural dynamics of magnetite (Fe3O4), we demonstrate that selecting specific electronic excitations with light allows these transitions to follow distinct pathways. Specifically, near-infrared photons (800 nm) that trigger d-d electronic transitions tend to dismantle the long-range zigzag network of trimerons, resulting in phase separation between cubic-metallic and monoclinic-insulating domains. Conversely, visible light (400 nm) enhances the long-range order of trimerons by stabilizing charge density wave fluctuations through oxygen 2p to iron 3d charge transfer excitations, thereby reinforcing the monoclinic insulating phase. These findings indicate that tailored light pulses can steer strongly correlated materials into various hidden phases, modulating the lifetimes and emergent properties of these intermediate states.

This discussion explores various experimental aspects of electron pair emission from surfaces through two distinct methodologies. The first approach utilizes an instrument featuring a pair of hemispherical analyzers driven by continuous beams of electrons or photons, whereas the second employs a pair of time-of-flight spectrometers necessitating a pulsed excitation source. A critical experimental parameter is the ratio of "true" to "random" coincidences, which can be evaluated using various techniques. Regardless of the specific instrument used, the primary flux must be significantly reduced compared to single-electron spectroscopy. We outline different strategies for achieving the necessary count rates, highlighting the concept of utilizing a delayed coincidence circuit. Furthermore, we examine methods for comparing the performance of these two spectrometer types.

We examine a system combining dynamical differential equations and qKZ difference equations, where the parameters align with those governing elliptic integrals. This system is solved modulo $p^n$ for any prime integer $p$ and any power $n$. We demonstrate that the $p$-adic limit of these solutions as $n \to \infty$ defines a sequence of line bundles; each bundle remains invariant under the associated dynamical connection, and the entire sequence is invariant under the corresponding qKZ difference connection.

By demonstrating that finite sums of power series can be expressed as the difference between two zeta functions, we validate the application of zeta functions with negative arguments in physical contexts to prevent the divergence of infinite sums. Specifically, we illustrate that for the magnetization of graphene, a zeta function with a negative variable emerges due to the energy cut-off separating two consecutive Landau levels. Moreover, this same line of reasoning can be extended to explain the zero-temperature Casimir force within a parallel-plate geometry.

We introduce a refined formulation of the Sato-Tate conjecture regarding the spacing distribution of angles associated with each prime number, and we examine its consequences for $L$-functions linked to elliptic curves within the context of random matrix theory.

This study introduces novel parameterized algorithms for the classical problem of determining if a directed acyclic graph possesses an upward planar drawing. The findings encompass a new fixed-parameter algorithm based on the count of sources, an XP-algorithm defined by treewidth, and another fixed-parameter algorithm utilizing treedepth. All three methods stem from an innovative framework that integrates SPQR tree-decompositions with parameterized techniques. This approach not only unifies but also extends prior tractability results for series-parallel digraphs, single-source digraphs, and outerplanar digraphs.

Legged locomotion systems, encompassing robots, exoskeletons, and prosthetics, demand actuators that combine low inertia with high output torque. While motor selection has traditionally focused on maximizing the motor gap radius, we introduce alternative, transmission-ratio-invariant metrics. These proposed criteria prioritize minimizing motor inertia and maximizing torque and motor constants without relying on gap radius, thereby achieving a more optimal balance of properties for legged applications. We rigorously evaluate the T-Motor RI50 and illustrate the utility of these metrics through a comparative case study against the commonly used T-Motor U8.

For over a century, scientists have gathered behavioral data, with an ever-growing portion now made publicly available for other researchers to reuse for replication, integration, or extension of prior findings. While this data is essential across numerous scientific disciplines, there is currently no widely accepted standard for its formatting, naming, organization, description, or sharing. This absence of standardization significantly hinders scientific advancement by obstructing effective data reuse and complicating data processing; non-standard data necessitates custom analysis code and stifles the creation of efficient tools. To solve this issue, we have developed the Behaverse Data Model (BDM), a standard designed to structure behavioral data. This paper focuses on core concepts within behavioral data, with further details and developments available on the project's website (https://behaverse.github.io/data-model/).

**Aims.** As optical wide-field telescopes accelerate their survey speeds and the need to detect transients at early stages grows, swift and dependable source localization has become critical. We introduce AutoSourceID-Light (ASID-L), a novel framework leveraging computer vision to efficiently process vast datasets and quickly pinpoint sources in optical imagery. **Methods.** Our ASID-L algorithm, which utilizes U-shaped networks augmented by a Laplacian of Gaussian filter (Chen et al. 1987), achieves superior localization accuracy. A U-Net (Ronneberger et al. 2015) identifies sources while filtering out various artifacts, subsequently passing the data to a Laplacian of Gaussian filter to determine precise coordinates. **Results.** Testing on MeerLICHT telescope optical images confirms the method's exceptional speed and localization capabilities. When compared to the standard SExtractor (Bertin & Arnouts 1996), our approach outperforms it, rapidly detecting more sources not only in sparse to moderately crowded fields but especially in regions exceeding 150 sources per square arcminute.

This study examines the Beris-Edwards system using both biaxial and uniaxial $Q$-tensors, employing a general Landau-de Gennes energy density characterized by four non-zero elastic constants. We establish the existence of strong solutions for the uniaxial case up to a maximal time. Additionally, we demonstrate that strong solutions corresponding to biaxial $Q$-tensors converge smoothly to those of the uniaxial system within the same maximal existence interval.

Tracking progress toward the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is crucial for both academic and non-academic entities. Current monitoring strategies have largely relied on specific data types, primarily publications within proprietary research databases. We introduce the `text2sdg` package for R, an accessible, open-source tool capable of identifying SDGs across diverse text formats using various existing or custom query systems. By supporting a broad range of text sources, this package not only enhances SDG monitoring but also establishes a vital foundation for validating and refining current methods of detecting SDGs within text.

We examine network evolution using `triplets`, defined as three-node graphlets. We propose a method to calculate a transition matrix that characterizes how these triplets evolve in temporal networks. To assess the significance of higher-order interactions, we compare artificial and real-world datasets against a model relying solely on pairwise interactions. The substantial discrepancies between the computed matrix and the one derived from fitted pairwise parameters indicate that non-pairwise interactions are present across various real-world systems in both space and time. Additionally, these findings reveal that distinct higher-order interaction patterns operate within different real-world scenarios.

To validate our approach, we employed these transition matrices as the foundation for a link prediction algorithm. We evaluated the algorithm's efficacy across four temporal networks, benchmarking it against ten alternative methods. Our results demonstrate that higher-order interactions in space and time are critical to network evolution; our method, alongside two other approaches based on non-local interactions, achieved the best overall performance. These outcomes further confirm that higher-order interaction patterns, specifically triplet dynamics, enhance our ability to understand and predict the evolution of diverse real-world systems.

Identifying less prominent features is essential for model compression, yet this aspect has not been explored within revolutionary attention mechanisms. This paper introduces a novel normalization-based attention module (NAM) designed to suppress less significant weights. By imposing a weight sparsity penalty on attention modules, NAM enhances computational efficiency without compromising performance. Evaluations against three other attention mechanisms on both ResNet and MobileNet demonstrate that our approach achieves superior accuracy. The code for this research is publicly available at https://github.com/Christian-lyc/NAM.

This study demonstrates that the inequality $t_m \leq \|\mathbf{A}\|_\infty \leq \sqrt{t_m}$ is valid for a Runge-Kutta matrix $\mathbf{A} \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times m}$ whose nodes stem from Gaussian quadrature, which integrates polynomials up to degree $2m-2$ exactly. This result also applies to Gauss-Lobatto quadrature. Furthermore, for a nonsingular matrix $\mathbf{A}$, its characteristic polynomial is given by $p_A(\lambda) = m!t^m + (m-1)!a_{m-1}t^{m-1} + \dots + a_0$, where the coefficients $a_i$ correspond to the polynomial $\omega(t) = (t - t_1) \dots (t - t_m) = t^m + a_{m-1}t^{m-1} + \dots + a_0$ associated with the nodes.

We demonstrate that the three-intensity protocol for measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (MDI QKD) can be implemented using varying light intensities within a single basis. Since the yields of single-photon pairs must be identical in both the $X$ and $Z$ bases, a lower bound established in one basis applies equally to the other. Because current MDI-QKD setups typically exhibit different yields across bases, our approach can significantly enhance the key rate by utilizing the lower bound of the yield in the advantageous basis. Furthermore, as our proposal employs fewer light intensities, it reduces the probability of intensity mismatch compared to existing protocols, thereby amplifying the method's benefits. We have numerically verified that selecting either the $Z$ or $X$ basis yields substantial improvements in key rates.

This chapter examines our recent efforts to generalize equilibrium (EQ) entropy to nonequilibrium (NEQ) systems, enabling the description of memory effects. By expanding the equilibrium state space through the introduction of internal variables, we account for irreversibility arising from internal processes. With a suitably chosen enlarged state space, the entropy functions as a state function that retains most properties of EQ entropy, differing only by the presence of nonzero irreversible entropy generation. We present both thermodynamic and statistical extensions of this entropy, demonstrating their equivalence via an appropriate state space definition. This approach yields a general, nonnegative statistical expression for entropy applicable to any scenario. Utilizing the statistical formulation, we establish the second law of thermodynamics. Furthermore, we provide examples to identify necessary internal variables and apply them to various cases of interest to compute entropy generation. Finally, we offer a potential explanation for the occurrence of negative entropy in the classical continuum 1-d Tonks gas by analyzing a lattice model where entropy remains strictly nonnegative.

A fundamental molecular and cellular comprehension of how SARS-CoV-2 differentially infects and leads to severe COVID-19 remains a critical hurdle in creating interventions to conclude the pandemic. To address this, we employed deep learning to analyze the biology of SARS-CoV-2 infection and disease severity by pinpointing transcriptomic signatures and cell types linked to infection and clinical outcomes. Specifically, we devised a novel method for generating self-supervised edge features. Our proposed model extends Graph Attention Networks (GAT) by creating these edge features through self-supervised learning and processing them via a Set Transformer. This architecture yields substantial gains in predicting individual cell disease states based on their transcriptomes. We applied our model to single-cell RNA sequencing data from SARS-CoV-2 infected lung organoids and bronchoalveolar lavage samples from COVID-19 patients, achieving state-of-the-art results on both datasets. Furthermore, leveraging explainable AI (XAI) techniques, we identified specific genes and cell types that distinguish bystander from infected cells over time and differentiate between moderate and severe disease. To our knowledge, this marks the first use of deep learning to uncover the molecular and cellular determinants of SARS-CoV-2 infection and COVID-19 severity using single-cell omics data.

Data-driven materials science, specifically Materials Informatics, is increasingly focusing on the automated retrieval of materials and their associated characteristics from scientific publications. This paper introduces Grobid-superconductors, a tool designed to automatically identify superconductor names and their corresponding properties from textual sources. Constructed as a Grobid extension, this solution integrates machine learning with heuristic methods within a multi-stage architecture capable of processing both raw text and PDF files. Leveraging Grobid-superconductors, we developed SuperCon2, a database containing 40,324 records of materials and properties derived from 37,700 papers. Each material entry is defined by its name, chemical formula, and class, with additional descriptors including shape, doping, component substitution variables, and substrate. The recorded properties feature the superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$) and, when applicable, the measurement method and applied pressure.

We review fundamental characteristics of the Beta distribution and its variations. Our analysis identified approximately 20 moment sequences of Beta distributions that correspond to significant integer sequences within the OEIS database, including Catalan, Riordan, Motzkin, and "super ballot" numbers. By utilizing a technique that expands the ratio of densities among the relevant distributions, we have derived numerous new relationships, alongside some established ones, linking these sequences—such as Catalan numbers—to other Beta distribution moment sequences.

This section details the LHCb measurements of time-dependent CP violation in charmless B meson decays, utilizing $p-p$ collision data acquired at a center-of-mass energy of 7 TeV during the 2010 and 2011 LHC runs. Specifically, we examine charmless two-body B decays, reporting direct and mixing-induced CP asymmetry terms for $B^{0}\to\pi^{+}\pi^{-}$ and $B_{s}^{0}\to K^{+}K^{-}$ based on 0.69 fb$^{-1}$ of data from 2011. Additionally, the branching ratio for $B_{s}^{0}\to K^{*0}\bar{K}^{*0}$ is presented, derived from 35 pb$^{-1}$ collected in 2010. Finally, the relative branching ratios for all $B_{(s)}^{0}\to K_S h^{+}h^{\prime -}$ decay modes (with $h^{(\prime)}=\pi,K$) are displayed, analyzed using 1 fb$^{-1}$ of data from 2011.

As machine learning (ML) systems become increasingly widespread, guaranteeing the fairness and equity of their core algorithms is critical. We contend that a viable strategy to achieve this is by actively generating public pressure on ML developers to create more equitable algorithms. Furthermore, we suggest that gaming offers a method to foster this public pressure while simultaneously aligning with the goals of algorithm developers. To illustrate this incentive-compatible approach, we introduce a new category of games termed "games for fairness and interpretability." These are meticulously crafted games designed for broad appeal; they are inherently engaging, illuminate the mechanics of machine learning models, and generate data that enables researchers and developers to refine their algorithms. We examine potential examples of such games, discuss their significance for fairness and interpretability, explain how their widespread adoption could generate constructive public pressure by bridging the divide between developers and the general public, and outline the advantages the machine learning community stands to gain.

Inspired by the theory of domination for types, we define a concept known as extension domination for Keisler measures. We demonstrate that this variation mirrors the behavior of its type-theoretic analogue. Our work establishes that extension domination generalizes type domination and constitutes a preorder on the space of global Keisler measures. Furthermore, we investigate fundamental properties of this notion, such as approximation by formulas, closure under localizations, and convex combinations. Finally, we present several preservation theorems alongside concrete examples.

Image-goal navigation presents a significant challenge, requiring agents to reach a target specified by an image within an unfamiliar environment. Existing approaches utilize various memory mechanisms to store navigation history for this purpose; however, they typically employ all stored observations to generate actions without distinguishing which portions are actually informative. To overcome this drawback, we introduce MemoNav, a new memory framework designed to enhance performance on multi-goal tasks by preserving only the agent's relevant short-term and long-term memories. Dynamic features on the agent's topological map are stored in short-term memory, while long-term memory is created by continuously aggregating short-term data through a graph attention module. A Transformer decoder-based forgetting module filters the short-term memory to retain only its informative subset, which is then combined with the long-term memory to form working memory used for action generation. Evaluated on a novel multi-goal navigation dataset, MemoNav significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods while utilizing a smaller fraction of navigation history. Furthermore, empirical results indicate that the model is less prone to deadlocks, validating that MemoNav improves navigation efficiency by minimizing redundant steps.

The even-even titanium isotopic series (A = 42 to 70) has been analyzed using the nuclear shell model with an effective Hamiltonian derived via many-body perturbation theory from a chiral potential incorporating two- and three-body forces. This Hamiltonian explicitly includes three-body terms to address Pauli principle violations in nuclei containing more than two valence particles. The calculations utilize $^{40}$Ca as a closed core and a model space defined by neutron and proton $0f_{1/2}$ orbitals, augmented by the $0g_{9/2}$ orbital for neutrons. Reported results include two-neutron separation energies and the excitation energies of the yrast $2^+$ states, which are compared against experimental data available up to $^{62}$Ti. This study aims to examine how the chosen effective interactions influence the evolution of shell structure.

This work aims to promote equitable and standardized evaluations of dose prediction methods for knowledge-based planning (KBP) within radiation therapy research. By organizing the 2020 AAPM Grand Challenge, OpenKBP, we invited participants to devise superior techniques for predicting doses from contoured CT images. Model performance was assessed using two distinct metrics: a dose score evaluating full 3D dose distributions, and a dose-volume histogram (DVH) score assessing specific DVH metrics. The study utilized data from 340 head-and-neck cancer patients treated with radiation, partitioned into training (n=200), validation (n=40), and testing (n=100) sets. During the validation phase, participants trained and refined their models on the provided datasets, while final rankings were determined in the testing phase based on out-of-sample performance. The challenge drew 195 participants from 28 countries; 73 individuals formed 44 teams during validation, submitting a total of 1750 entries, with the testing phase receiving submissions from 28 teams. On average, models improved their dose and DVH scores by factors of 2.7 and 5.7, respectively, throughout the validation period. In the final testing phase, one model outperformed all others significantly in both dose and DVH metrics. Many top-performing teams attributed their success to generalizable techniques, such as ensembles. As the inaugural competition for KBP research, OpenKBP established the first platform for fair and consistent method comparison. Furthermore, the publicly released OpenKBP datasets facilitate future benchmarking, effectively democratizing KBP research by increasing accessibility for all.

As China's mobile population grows, its fertility rate remains well below the level required for stable generational replacement, drawing significant concern regarding human resource supply imbalances. Drawing on data from the 2018 National Mobile Population Dynamics Monitoring Survey, this study employs LPM and Probit models to assess how housing costs influence the fertility intentions of mobile residents. To address potential endogeneity, the lagged land sales price serves as an instrumental variable for housing prices. The findings indicate that a 100% increase in the ratio of housing prices to household income reduces the fertility intentions of working-age women in their destination by 4.42%, with a marginal effect of EXP(-0.222). Furthermore, infrastructure development at the inflow location moderates the sensitivity of fertility intentions to housing costs. Working-age female migrants who are younger, have smaller families, and possess higher education levels demonstrate a stronger willingness to have children in their new locations. Ultimately, these insights offer a novel practical perspective for advancing institutional reforms and achieving balanced economic development during China's current economic transition.

This paper introduces a novel inverse photoemission setup featuring a low-energy electron source with spin and angle resolution. The compact spin-polarized source enables the independent control of the spin polarization vector and the electron beam propagation vector, facilitating the investigation of any spin orientation across all wavevectors. Using a shielded electron optical system, the beam polarization can be adjusted to any desired direction while maintaining a parallel beam configuration. The system's capabilities were validated through measurements on Cu(001) and Au(111) surfaces. At room temperature, the overall energy resolution is estimated at approximately 170 meV, derived from the $k_{B}T_{eff}$ of the Cu(001) Fermi level, enabling direct comparison with photoemission data. The setup's spin-resolved functionality was confirmed by observing the Rashba splitting of the Au(111) Shockley surface state. With an effective electron beam polarization of $P=30\pm3$ \% and a wavevector resolution of $\Delta k_{F}\lesssim0.06$ \AA$^{-1}$, studies on the Au(111) surface state illustrate the ability to tune the electron beam polarization direction within three spatial dimensions. Maximum spin asymmetry was achieved when the electron beam polarization aligned with the in-plane spin polarization of the Au(111) surface state.

This paper introduces a construction for modeling shared-variable systems using higher-dimensional automata (HDAs) that is compositional: parallel compositions of independent systems are represented by the standard tensor product of HDAs, while nondeterministic choice is modeled via the coproduct.

This study examines a single-echelon, periodic review inventory system with two suppliers and stochastic demand, assuming that unmet demand is backlogged. The expedited supplier offers a shorter lead time but at a higher unit cost compared to the regular supplier. We propose the Projected Expedited Inventory Position (PEIP) policy and demonstrate that, as both the shortage cost and the cost premium for expedited units increase (while maintaining a constant ratio), the relative difference between the long-run average cost of PEIP and the optimal policy approaches zero. This finding implies that several existing heuristics are also asymptotically optimal within this non-trivial regime. Furthermore, extensive numerical analysis reveals that the PEIP policy surpasses the best-performing heuristic policies currently available in the literature.

This study reports measurements of the first through fourth moments of the squared lepton mass, $q^2$, for \mbox{$B \to X_c \, \ell\, \bar \nu_{\ell}$} decays involving electrons and muons, where $X_c$ represents a hadronic system with a charm quark. The analysis utilizes data from electron-positron collisions at the $\Upsilon(4S)$ resonance, amounting to $62.8 \, \mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity gathered by the Belle II experiment in 2019 and 2020. To isolate the $X_c$ system and determine $q^2$, one $B$ meson from an $\Upsilon(4S) \to B \kern 0.18em\overline{\kern -0.18em B}$ decay is fully reconstructed via a hadronic mode using a multivariate $B$ tagging algorithm. We provide both raw and central moments for the kinematic ranges $q^2 > 1.5 \; \mathrm{GeV^2/c^4}$ and $q^2 > 8.5 \; \mathrm{GeV^2/c^4}$, covering up to 77% of the accessible phase space for \mbox{$B \to X_c \, \ell\, \bar \nu_{\ell}$}. Notably, this represents the first measurement of such moments in the experimentally difficult interval of $[ 1.5, 2.5 ] \, \mathrm{GeV^2/c^4}$.

Sudoku puzzles typically feature a consistent pattern in their initial digits and are designed to be solved using established strategies. This paper addresses the generation of such instances by introducing a rigorous framework to evaluate solvability based on specific strategies, accommodating both known methods and general strategies under reasonable assumptions. We propose an exact algorithm to determine clues for a predefined set of positions that ensures solvability using a given strategy set; to our knowledge, this is the first exact method aside from trivial brute-force approaches. Beyond clue generation, we apply this method to identify the minimum number of clues required for a strategy-solvable Sudoku. Experimental evaluations, varying clue positions and counts randomly, demonstrate that the method completes within one minute for many grids. However, as the clue count approaches 20, execution time rises sharply, surpassing a 600-second limit. Additionally, we tested the method on instances with 17 clues derived from known minimal Sudokus to assess its efficiency in detecting unsolvability.

Large-scale language models like GPT-3 have demonstrated remarkable capabilities across diverse tasks, including text summarization. This paper extends that observation to the domain of opinion summarization. We investigate multiple pipeline strategies for applying GPT-3 to zero-shot summarize extensive collections of user reviews, focusing on recursive summarization and methods that select salient content via supervised clustering or extraction. Across two datasets—an aspect-oriented hotel review set and a generic summarization set comprising Amazon and Yelp reviews—our results indicate that GPT-3 achieves superior performance in human evaluations. We contend that conventional metrics fail to capture these strengths and instead assess several novel measures targeting faithfulness, factuality, and genericity to compare the different approaches.

This paper details measurements of beam backgrounds conducted during the 2016 initial commissioning phase of the SuperKEKB collider using the CLAWS detector system, which utilizes plastic scintillators and silicon photomultipliers. The sensors' single-particle detection capability and sub-nanosecond time resolution facilitate bunch-by-bunch measurements, enabling a novel time-resolved analysis of beam backgrounds and making the system ideal for investigating injection backgrounds. We present data on various aspects of both regular and injection backgrounds, covering time structure, decay behavior, hit-energy spectra, and overall background rates. These results indicate that elevated background rates following an injection typically persist for several milliseconds, with most particles detected within the first 500 microseconds. Furthermore, injection backgrounds display distinct temporal patterns linked to betatron and synchrotron oscillations within the accelerator rings, with pattern frequencies derived directly from detector data.

Although end-to-end dialogue generation has shown promising results by avoiding handcrafted features and task-specific attributes, a critical limitation is its inability to produce informative utterances, thereby restricting its applicability in certain real-world conversational systems. This paper proposes a variational generation model equipped with a joint attention mechanism that conditions responses on both dialogue context and external knowledge to generate diverse and informative outputs.

By assigning an order to the underlying alphabet, we can extend this ordering to the states of a finite deterministic automaton (DFA) by comparing the strings that lead to them. When the string order is co-lexicographic and total, the resulting DFA is termed a Wheeler automaton. This recently defined class of automata serves as a crucial data structure for languages, enabling highly efficient storage mechanisms for transition functions that support diverse substring queries.

In this context, it is natural to examine the class of regular languages accepted by Wheeler automata, known as Wheeler languages. A significant finding in this domain is that, unlike the general case, the standard determinization via the powerset construction runs in polynomial time for Wheeler automata. Consequently, most classical problems solvable on this class are "easy," meaning they can be resolved in polynomial time.

This paper investigates computational problems related to Wheelerness starting from non-deterministic automata. We also analyze reduced non-deterministic automata (NFA), a subset where recognizing Wheelerness remains polynomial, similar to DFAs. Our findings demonstrate that transitioning to non-determinism is often problematic, quickly leading to intractability in most scenarios.

Furthermore, we initiate a study on "state complexity" concerning Wheeler DFAs and languages, proving that the classic construction for language intersection is computationally more efficient for Wheeler DFAs than in the general case. Additionally, we present a construction for the minimal Wheeler DFA that recognizes a specific Wheeler language.

Creating natural head movements synchronized with speech is essential for delivering a rich interactive experience in embodied conversational agents. While previous research typically evaluates generated motion quality by comparing it to a single ground-truth reference using objective metrics, this approach overlooks the existence of many plausible motion sequences for a given utterance. This study examines the perceptual quality variations among head motions sampled from a generative model. Our findings reveal that even when a model produces diverse motions, the resulting perceptual quality varies significantly. Furthermore, we demonstrate that standard objective metrics used in prior studies fail to accurately capture this perceptual quality. These results suggest a promising direction for future research: developing objective metrics that better align with human perception of quality.

We examine the problem of determining when an orientable closed 4-manifold $Y$ is dominated by another such manifold $X$, with specific attention to instances where $X$ is either geometric or admits a non-trivial fibration over an orientable surface.

To enhance cellular system capacity, operators have historically deployed 4G LTE small cells (Femto Cells) by reusing licensed spectrum. However, this licensed spectrum is no longer sufficient to meet the demands of future applications such as augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR). Consequently, operators have turned to unlicensed spectrum in the Wi-Fi 5 GHz band, which 3GPP later designated as LTE Licensed Assisted Access (LAA). The ongoing and recent LAA rollouts in developed regions like the US offer a valuable opportunity to examine the ground truth of coexistence dynamics. This paper provides a high-level overview of my past, present, and future research regarding the benefits of small cells. Looking ahead, the focus will shift to the newest unlicensed band, the 6 GHz spectrum, where the latest Wi-Fi standard, 802.11ax, will coexist with the most advanced cellular technology, 5G New Radio (NR).

When numerous similar entities interact at a microscopic level, both with one another and their surroundings, unpredictable patterns can spontaneously manifest at larger spatial and temporal scales. This phenomenon, termed emergence, defines a wide array of complex systems ranging from physical to biological and social domains, frequently manifesting as collective behavior. It is pervasive, observable in non-living systems like synchronizing oscillators and living ones such as bird flocks or fish schools. Although there is substantial empirical evidence confirming the existence of emergent properties, fundamental theoretical questions persist, including the absence of a universally accepted rigorous definition and the unclear identification of the specific physical conditions that promote emergence. This article provides a comprehensive overview of emergence and outlines both current and future challenges within the field. Furthermore, this review serves as an introduction to the Theme Issue "Emergent phenomena in complex physical and socio-technical systems: from cells to societies," where we synthesize the issue's contents, connect them to these ongoing challenges, and explore topics spanning from the origins of life to the large-scale spread of infectious diseases.

This paper introduces a novel extension of Serrin's celebrated lower semicontinuity theorem for the variational functional $\int_{\Omega}f(x,u,u')dx$. We establish its lower semicontinuity within $W_{loc}^{1,1}(\Omega)$ under the strong $L_{loc}^{1}$ topology, provided the integrand $f(x,s,\xi)$ exhibits standard continuity across all three variables, convexity with respect to $\xi$, and local absolute continuity regarding $x$.

This work examines the message complexity of State Machine Replication protocols operating under Byzantine failures within a partial synchrony framework. While Dolev and Reischuk established a quadratic lower bound for this complexity, it remained unclear if this bound was tight, as the most efficient protocols known at the time exhibited a worst-case complexity of $O(n^3)$. We present a protocol that achieves Dolev and Reischuk's quadratic lower bound while maintaining other essential properties. In a system with $n$ replicas where $f$ exhibit Byzantine faults (assuming $n \geq 3f+1$), and given $\Delta$ as the upper bound on message delay (meaning a message sent at time $t$ arrives by $\text{max} \{ t, GST \} +\Delta$), our deterministic protocol simultaneously delivers $O(n^2)$ worst-case message complexity, optimistic responsiveness, $O(f\Delta)$ time for the first confirmation after Global Stabilization Time (GST), and $O(n)$ mean message complexity.

This paper investigates rational twisted power series defined over a commutative field. We provide multiple characterizations of these series that mirror classical findings regarding rational power series over such fields. Notably, we establish a version of Kronecker's lemma applicable to the rationality of twisted power series.

Assessing the safety of human body orientation is a critical challenge in human-robot interaction. Understanding dynamic physical constraints on human movement enhances the detection of safe motions, providing vital data on the stability and normality of postures alongside real-time risk evaluation. Additionally, this data enables cooperative robots and monitoring systems to interact more freely within the environment, while known safety characteristics allow for a more deterministic definition of the workspace. Driven by these motivations, we introduce a novel Predictive Safety Model (PSM) that utilizes inertial measurement unit data from the human chest. The PSM incorporates a 3-degree-of-freedom spring-damper pendulum model to forecast human motion using a safe motion dataset. By integrating a safety dataset with an elastic spring-damper model, the approach determines estimated safe human orientations, capable of executing complex movements across varying safety levels. Experiments conducted in real-world scenarios validate this proposed model. This methodology offers significant potential for guidance and assistive robots, as well as health monitoring systems, to support and evaluate human conditions, especially for the elderly.

The World Robotics Challenge (2018 and 2020) aimed to task teams with creating systems capable of adapting easily to new missions and maintaining robust performance within semi-structured environments. This work introduces a layered approach for converting missions into actionable tasks, alongside specific strategies to handle both simple and complex failures. We propose a failure characterization model that guides repair discussions. Simple failures occurred most frequently in our WRC system, and we detail the methods used to address them.

International trade stands as a foundational domain within economic research. Today, the abundance of available data allows analysts to enhance traditional methods with advanced techniques that transcend conventional approaches. This study demonstrates the application of Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) models—a prominent method from Natural Language Processing—to uncover hidden dimensions within the international trade product space and track their distribution across nations over time. Utilizing a dataset of goods exports spanning from 1962 to 2016, the research reveals the ability to create higher-level classifications of products grounded in empirical evidence, while also examining how these categories are distributed among countries. These results provide valuable insights into the patterns of national trade specialization.

In image aesthetic quality evaluation, the normal distribution of aesthetic datasets makes it challenging to capture samples from both high and low score regions, leading to labeling errors. To address this distribution issue and improve labeling accuracy, we introduce AMD-CR, a novel mixed dataset designed for both classification and regression tasks. We train a meta-reweighting network to apply differential loss weighting to the training data. Furthermore, we implement a stage-specific training strategy that leverages pseudo-labels from a binary classification task to guide subsequent aesthetic training in both classification and regression phases. Regarding network architecture, we develop an Aesthetic Adaptive Block (AAB) capable of handling input images of any size and incorporate Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) to enhance feature extraction for each task. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves a 0.1112 improvement in SROCC compared to conventional methods. Additionally, this method facilitates optimal aesthetic path planning for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and ground vehicles.

This paper presents a novel sensor-driven control strategy that manages heat exchange between a radiative source and a target object through robot movements. This sensorimotor ability is crucial for various industrial, dermatological, and field robotics applications and serves as a foundational element for developing machines with advanced thermo-motor intelligence. Consequently, we develop a geometric-thermal-motor model that defines the link between the robot's active configuration and the resulting dynamic thermal response. Utilizing this model, we designed two new thermal servoing controllers—one model-based and one adaptive—and assessed their stability using Lyapunov theory. To validate the proposed approach, we conducted a comprehensive experimental study featuring a robotic manipulator performing autonomous thermal servoing tasks. As far as we are aware, this work represents the first instance where temperature regulation has been framed as a motion control problem for robots.

This paper introduces a differential protection scheme for a distribution line linking a wind farm within a microgrid. Machine Learning (ML) models are developed using differential features derived from currents at both line terminals to support relaying decisions. After selecting from a comprehensive feature set, wavelet coefficients are utilized to train the classifiers, which effectively differentiate internal faults, including high impedance faults (HIFs) with minimal current, from external faults and CT saturation issues. Simulations conducted in a 5-bus PSCAD/EMTDC system demonstrate that these ML-based approaches can reliably distinguish faults and transients, thereby ensuring the security and dependability of microgrid operations.

We demonstrate that an observation of the lepton flavor violating $\mu \rightarrow e \gamma$ process in the MEG II experiment would allow constraints on the initial density of primordial black holes (PBHs) within the framework of scotogenic dark matter. Specifically, if PBH evaporation takes place during the radiation-dominated era, the initial density parameter $\beta$ (defined as the ratio of PBH density $\rho_{\rm PBH}$ to radiation density $\rho_{\rm rad}$ at formation) is constrained to the range $2\times 10^{-17} \lesssim \beta \lesssim 3 \times 10^{-16}$ for a dark sector at the $\mathcal{O}$(TeV) scale. Alternatively, if evaporation occurs in the PBH-dominated era, the initial density may fall between $1 \times 10^{-8} \lesssim \beta \lesssim 3 \times 10^{-7}$ for $\mathcal{O}$(GeV) scale dark matter accompanied by other $\mathcal{O}$(TeV) scale particles in the scotogenic model.

Since the 1960s, Mastermind has been investigated for its combinatorial and information-theoretic significance, yielding numerous results. Erdős and Rényi initially established the optimal number of queries for a two-color scenario. Chvátal later derived asymptotically optimal bounds for $k$ colors and $n$ positions when $k \le n^{1-\epsilon}$. After a series of incremental improvements addressing cases where $k \ge n$, the primary unresolved issue has been bridging the gap between $\Omega(n)$ and $\mathcal{O}(n\log \log n)$ for $k=n$. This paper resolves that gap by introducing the first algorithm capable of solving $k=n$ Mastermind using a linear number of queries. Consequently, we now establish the query complexity of Mastermind for all parameter values of $k$ and $n$.

Humans are capable of categorizing novel entities by reasoning through their linguistic descriptions, a skill rooted in language's compositional structure that allows the synthesis of known concepts to define new ones. For instance, defining "mavens" as "large birds with black feathers" enables others to identify them by combining their existing knowledge of "large birds" and "black feathers." Motivated by this, our work addresses zero-shot classification by logically parsing and reasoning over natural language explanations. We introduce CLORE (Classification by LOgical Reasoning on Explanations), a framework that, unlike prior methods treating text as implicit features, decomposes explanations into logical structures and reasons along them to generate classification scores. Experiments on explanation-based zero-shot benchmarks show that CLORE outperforms baselines, particularly in tasks demanding significant logical reasoning. Beyond providing classification outcomes, CLORE offers the underlying logical parsing and reasoning as an interpretable rationale. Furthermore, empirical analysis reveals that CLORE is more robust against linguistic biases compared to baseline approaches.

This paper investigates the phenomenon of large intersections within the context of multiple recurrence for measure-preserving actions of countable abelian groups. Key findings include: (1) For a countable abelian group $G$ and homomorphisms $\varphi, \psi : G \to G$ where $\varphi(G)$, $\psi(G)$, and $(\psi - \varphi)(G)$ possess finite index in $G$, it holds that for any ergodic measure-preserving system $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, (T_g)_{g \in G})$, any set $A \in \mathcal{B}$, and any $\varepsilon > 0$, the set $\{g \in G : \mu(A \cap T_{\varphi(g)}^{-1}A \cap T_{\psi(g)}^{-1}A) > \mu(A)^3 - \varepsilon\}$ is syndetic. (2) Similarly, if $G$ is a countable abelian group and integers $r, s$ satisfy the condition that $rG$, $sG$, and $(r \pm s)G$ have finite index in $G$, then for every ergodic measure-preserving system $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, (T_g)_{g \in G})$, every set $A \in \mathcal{B}$, and every $\varepsilon > 0$, the set $\{g \in G : \mu(A \cap T_{rg}^{-1}A \cap T_{sg}^{-1}A \cap T_{(r+s)g}^{-1}A) > \mu(A)^4 - \varepsilon\}$ is syndetic. These results extend and generalize prior work by Bergelson, Host, and Kra on $\mathbb{Z}$-actions, as well as findings by Bergelson, Tao, and Ziegler regarding $\mathbb{F}_p^{\infty}$-actions. By applying an ergodic variant of the Furstenberg correspondence principle, we derive new combinatorial applications. Additionally, we examine numerous examples that illuminate the necessity of the stated hypotheses. Finally, our findings prompt several intriguing questions and conjectures, which are presented in the introduction and conclusion.

We apply the newly developed resummation method, renormalization group optimized perturbation theory (RGOPT), to calculate the equation of state (EoS) for non-strange cold quark matter at next-to-leading order (NLO). Drawing on recent findings that stable quark matter likely consists solely of up and down quarks, we evaluate the mass-radius relationship for two-flavor pure quark stars and contrast these results with next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) perturbative QCD (pQCD) predictions. This comparison demonstrates that by incorporating renormalization group properties and a variational optimization procedure, RGOPT enables efficient resummation of the perturbative series. Notably, selecting the renormalization scale to match the mass of pulsar PSR J0740+6620 ($M= 2.08\pm 0.07 M_\odot$) yields a mass-radius curve that also accurately predicts the masses and radii of pulsar PSR J0030+0451 and compact object HESS J1731-347. Furthermore, the scale dependence of both the EoS and the mass-radius relation derived via RGOPT shows significant improvement over that of pQCD. This pioneering application to quark stars indicates that RGOPT serves as a robust alternative to pQCD for modeling compressed quark matter.

We investigate weightings, also known as quasi-homogeneous structures, that emerge from manifolds equipped with singular Lie filtrations. This approach extends the constructions developed by Choi-Ponge, Van Erp-Yuncken, and Haj-Higson for the case of regular Lie filtrations.

Cycles in a graph induce a natural cyclic arrangement of their edge sets, with these arrangements being consistent because two edges are adjacent in a cycle if and only if they are adjacent in every cycle containing both.
