Coupling superconducting microwave resonators with rare earth-doped crystals offers a promising hybrid quantum platform for applications such as spin-based transducers and memory. The efficiency of this interaction is quantified by cooperativity, which measures the coupling strength between microwave photons and rare earth ion spins. In this study, we demonstrate an ultra-high cooperativity of approximately $C \sim$ 650 between erbium spins in yttrium orthosilicate and a planar superconducting microwave resonator. This device utilizes a highly uniform magnetic field to exploit the strong anisotropic coupling inherent to the material. Achieving cooperativity levels comparable to those of bulk dielectric resonators, this work establishes a viable route for efficiently integrating spin-photon coupling onto a compact platform.

We demonstrate that for conformal field theories with $d\geq 3$ and at least 4 supercharges, conformal manifolds are K\"ahler-Hodge. This finding extends earlier results established for 4d ${\cal N}=2$ and ${\cal N}=4$ theories, as well as various 2d SCFTs, to the cases of 3d ${\cal N}=2$ and 4d ${\cal N}=1$. In superconformal field theories, conformal manifolds carry a holomorphic line bundle ${\cal L}$ that represents operator mixing among supercharges during marginal deformations. By applying conformal perturbation theory and superconformal Ward identities, we calculate the curvature of ${\cal L}$ at an arbitrary point on the manifold. We establish that the K\"ahler form of the Zamolodchikov metric is proportional to the first Chern class of ${\cal L}$, where the proportionality constant is the stress tensor two-point function coefficient, $C_T$. Furthermore, under specific conditions regarding singular points on the conformal manifold, this relationship leads to a quantization condition for the manifold's total volume.

We introduce Sliced Recursive Transformer (SReT), a novel and efficient vision transformer design that leverages a simple yet effective recursive operation to enhance parameter utilization without adding extra parameters. This approach is realized by sharing weights across the depth of the network. Using a straightforward recursive strategy yields a significant accuracy gain of approximately 2%, requires no specialized design expertise, and incurs minimal computational overhead during training. To mitigate the extra computation from recursion while preserving high accuracy, we propose an approximation method utilizing multiple sliced group self-attentions across recursive layers, which cuts computational costs by 10–30% with negligible performance degradation. SReT is compatible with various existing efficient ViT architectures. Our top-performing model achieves substantial improvements on ImageNet-1K over state-of-the-art methods while using fewer parameters. The proposed sliced recursive weight-sharing mechanism enables the construction of transformers with over 100 to 1,000 shared layers easily, maintaining a compact size of 13–15M parameters and avoiding optimization issues associated with overly large models. This flexible scalability demonstrates strong potential for building extremely deep vision transformers. The code is accessible at https://github.com/szq0214/SReT.

During the epoch of reionization, a portion of galactic Ly$\alpha$ radiation is scattered within the intergalactic medium (IGM), manifesting as diffuse light that stretches megaparsecs away from its source. We explore methods to utilize this scattered light to study the characteristics of early galaxies and their adjacent IGM. By developing a Monte Carlo algorithm that tracks individual photons, we replicate various test scenarios from existing literature and subsequently apply our code to the simulated IGM of the CoDaII project. Our findings indicate that collecting scattered light over areas spanning several square arcminutes can leave a detectable signature on the emergent spectrum. While scattering tends to redden emission by lengthening photon paths, it can also produce bluer photons via upscattering driven by the peculiar motions of scatterers. Notably, photons emitted on the far blue side of the resonance exhibit greater extension in both frequency and space compared to those near the resonance, offering a distinctive feature for blueward emission that direct, unscattered light from the source cannot constrain. Additionally, the IGM's ionization state influences the scattered light spectrum; when a source resides in a small HII region, the emission undergoes more scatterings within the surrounding neutral hydrogen (HI) region regardless of initial frequency, resulting in greater redshifting and spatial extension. This process may lead to a reduction in scattered light intensity toward higher redshifts during reionization. Ultimately, our results establish a framework for interpreting scattered light data expected from high-redshift integral-field-unit surveys.

Location data is anticipated to be fundamental for enabling communication and context-aware services within 6G networks. User localization relies on estimating delay and/or angles via uplink or downlink pilot signals; however, hardware impairments (HWIs) distort signals at both transmitter and receiver ends, thereby degrading localization accuracy. Although this effect may be negligible at lower frequencies where HWIs are milder, 6G necessitates rigorous modeling and analysis to assess the resulting performance loss. This study models various impairment types and performs a misspecified Cramér-Rao bound analysis to quantify HWI-induced degradation. Simulation results across different HWI categories demonstrate that each impairment type causes distinct levels of deterioration in both angle and delay estimation performance.

This paper investigates the complementarity spectrum of directed graphs, focusing specifically on characterizing these structures via their spectrum. The central inquiry addresses whether non-isomorphic digraphs sharing the same vertex count can possess identical complementarity eigenvalues. These eigenvalues, alternatively known as Pareto eigenvalues, have driven research into the complementarity spectra of undirected graphs; notably, characterizing undirected graphs solely through these eigenvalues remains an unresolved issue. We provide characterizations for digraphs possessing one and two complementarity eigenvalues, and we present examples of non-isomorphic digraphs that share the same complementarity spectrum.

In complex video action recognition, the efficacy of the designed model is paramount. However, manually crafted network architectures typically depend heavily on a researcher's expertise and intuition. Consequently, Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has gained significant traction in recent years due to its automated design capabilities, achieving notable success in image processing. Although some image-based NAS techniques have minimized GPU search time to single digits, applying standard 3D convolutions to extend NAS to video analysis often results in an explosion of computational costs. To overcome this hurdle, we introduce a novel framework termed Neural Architecture Search-Temporal Convolution (NAS-TC). This framework operates in two distinct phases: initially, a classical CNN serves as the backbone to handle computationally demanding feature extraction, followed by a lightweight stitching search on the cell to capture long-range temporal dependencies. This two-stage approach ensures efficient parameter allocation and enables the processing of minute-level videos. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves competitive recognition accuracy.

This work proposes methods for identifying 1-factorizations $F$ in girth-regular graphs characterized by a specific girth, regular degree, and chromatic index $g$, specifically for scenarios where every girth cycle intersects each 1-factor within $F$. These approaches are relevant to priority assignment tasks, managerial optimization, and decision-making processes. Furthermore, the study explores applications to hamiltonian decomposability—achieved through the union of pairs of 1-factors—and to three-dimensional geometry, including M\"obius-strip compounds and hollow-triangle polylinks.

We report findings from our investigation of the close pre-main sequence spectroscopic binary CVSO 104 in Ori OB1, utilizing data from the PENELLOPE legacy program. For the first time, we have determined the system's orbital elements and the stellar parameters for both components. The system consists of two early M-type stars with an orbital period of approximately 5 days and a mass ratio of 0.92; notably, contrary to expectations, no tertiary companion is detected. Although both stars exhibit quasi-synchronization, the orbit remains highly eccentric. The spectral energy distribution indicates a substantial infrared excess, suggesting the presence of a circumbinary disk. After subtracting the composite photospheric spectrum, our analysis of HeI and Balmer line profiles shows that both stars are accreting at comparable rates. Additionally, we detect excess emission in H$\alpha$ and H$\beta$ that is redshifted or blueshifted by over 100 km/s relative to the system's mass center, varying with orbital phase; this emission may originate from accretion structures like funnels feeding from the circumbinary disk. Furthermore, we examined an optical companion located roughly 2".4 away, which we designate as CVSO 104B. This object is a background Sun-like star not physically linked to the pre-main sequence system and is not a member of Ori OB1.

For graphs $H$ and $F$, the generalized Turán number $ex(n,H,F)$ denotes the maximum number of copies of $H$ that can exist in an $F$-free graph with $n$ vertices. We define $H$ as $F$-Turán-good when, for sufficiently large $n$, $ex(n,H,F)$ equals the count of $H$ copies in the $(\chi(F)-1)$-partite Turán graph. This work establishes a general theorem applicable when $F$ contains an edge whose removal reduces its chromatic number. Specifically, it exactly determines $ex(n,P_k,C_{2\ell+1})$ and $ex(n,C_{2k},C_{2\ell+1})$ for large $n$. Additionally, the study examines scenarios where $F$ possesses a vertex whose deletion lowers the chromatic number.

We introduce the inaugural azimuthally differential measurements of the pion source size relative to the second harmonic event plane in Pb-Pb collisions at a center-of-mass energy per nucleon-nucleon pair of $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=2.76$ TeV. These measurements were conducted within the 0-50% centrality range and for pion pair transverse momenta spanning $0.2 < k_{\rm T} < 0.7$ GeV/$c$. Our results reveal that the $R_{\rm side}$ and $R_{\rm out}$ radii—describing the pion source dimensions perpendicular and parallel to the pion transverse momentum, respectively—oscillate out of phase, a pattern consistent with observations from the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC). The final-state source eccentricity, derived from $R_{\rm side}$ oscillations, is notably smaller than the initial-state eccentricity yet remains positive; this suggests that despite a more pronounced expansion along the in-plane direction, the pion source at freeze-out retains an elongation in the out-of-plane direction. While 3+1D hydrodynamic simulations qualitatively match the observed centrality and transverse momentum $R_{\rm side}$ oscillations, they consistently underestimate the magnitude of these oscillations.

Mobile manipulators, which integrate both mobility and dexterity, are increasingly deployed for unstructured field applications such as vineyards. Consequently, the coordinated movement of the mobile base and the manipulator is critical for overall system performance. This paper investigates a whole-body motion controller for a non-holonomic wheeled mobile manipulator (NWMM), consisting of a 2-DoF wheeled base and a 7-DoF arm, specifically designed to efficiently handle complex grapevine pruning. Within the control framework, task-priority-based coordinated motion is ensured by projecting lower-priority tasks into the null space of higher-priority ones, thereby allowing high-priority objectives to be executed without interruption. The efficacy of the proposed controller was validated through a grapevine spur pruning experiment.

This paper presents three novel findings regarding the axiomatization of the core for characteristic function games, which do not necessarily feature transferable utility, provided the set of individually rational payoff vectors is bounded. A key distinction of this work is that it applies to the complete class of such games, eliminating the need for additional constraints such as "non-levelness" or "balancedness."

Using the nonperturbative functional renormalization group, we investigate the critical behavior of the one-dimensional random field Ising model (RFIM) characterized by long-range interactions decaying as $r^{-(d+\sigma)}$. Our analysis reveals two distinct critical regimes governed by the parameter $\sigma$, which are divided by a critical threshold $\sigma_c$. The defining feature separating these regimes is the existence or absence of a cusp-like nonanalyticity in the functional form of the renormalized random field cumulants at the fixed point. This shift in behavior correlates with the properties of large-scale avalanches occurring in the system at zero temperature. We outline methods for validating these predictions via lattice simulations and compare our findings with the RFIM defined on the Dyson hierarchical lattice.

This study introduces a new adaptive search space decomposition technique alongside a gradient-free optimization framework designed for pre- and post-buckling analysis of space truss structures. Frequently utilized in structural engineering for large-scale steel applications like bridges and domes, these structures experience significant displacements, making them susceptible to sudden failures caused by progressive collapses from local or global buckling. The proposed approach enables the analysis of load-equilibrium paths under both variable and permanent loading conditions, accounting for stable and unstable equilibrium phases while explicitly addressing geometric nonlinearities. The primary objective is to identify these equilibrium stages by optimizing the system's Lagrangian kinematic parameters to establish global equilibrium. However, this optimization is complex due to the undefined parameter domain and the sensitivity and interdependencies among Lagrangian variables. Consequently, the problem is formulated as a nonlinear, multimodal, unconstrained, continuous optimization task. A novel adaptive search space decomposition method is developed to progressively redefine the search domain (a hypersphere), allowing a gradient-free optimization algorithm to evaluate system equilibrium. The methodology is validated through three benchmark problems and a medium-sized test case representing a real-world structural scenario. By comparing results regarding displacement-load curves and deformed configurations with existing literature, the study demonstrates the high accuracy and robustness of the proposed method, highlighting the significant potential of gradient-free algorithms for analyzing space truss structures.

Decision trees serve as adaptable predictive models designed to map relationships between outcomes and covariates while identifying key population subgroups. Yet, traditional graphical depictions of fitted trees emphasize specific split points, making them less effective for visualizing defined subgroups. This paper introduces a new visualization approach that prioritizes subgroup characterization, detailing both their defining covariates and outcome distributions. We have implemented this method in the \texttt{visTree} package, which leverages the infrastructure of the \texttt{partykit} package to support visualization across various decision tree types. The package's individual functions are illustrated using data from the Box Lunch study [French et al., 2014], a randomized trial assessing how varying lunch sizes impact energy intake and body weight in working adults.

Many engineering, scientific, and computational issues remain unsolved due to a lack of computationally efficient methods. A growing challenge lies in the shift of evolving technologies toward autonomy and intelligent decision-making, a trend that generates vast quantities of data from diverse sources like cameras, smartphones, health monitors, smart meters, and environmental sensors. Consequently, there is an urgent need to create efficient algorithms for data generation, analysis, classification, and visualization. Data is often organized purposefully through structures such as large-scale networks and graphs. This text centers on data science, specifically addressing the "curse of dimensionality" (CoD) resulting from the sheer volume of collected data. This challenge drives researchers to explore optimization strategies using nature-inspired meta-heuristics, such as evolutionary algorithms (EAs), which, despite their non-deterministic nature, are robust enough to find optimal solutions. Researchers typically turn to EAs only when standard methods get trapped in local optima rather than reaching the global optimum. In this chapter, we first establish a formal definition of the CoD problem, then examine feature extraction techniques and their categories, followed by a general overview of meta-heuristic algorithms, their terminology, and the desirable properties of evolutionary approaches.

Liquid water exhibits fascinating thermodynamic anomalies in its supercooled state, which phenomenological two-state models—grounded in the hypothesis of two competing local structures—have effectively explained. Despite this success, the specific structural characteristics of these competing states remain unclear. In this study, we utilize a geometrical, order-parameter-free method to definitively distinguish between two types of competing local states in TIP4P/2005 liquid water: one energetically favored and the other entropically favored, both displaying distinct structural and energetic properties. This distinction arises from analyzing the heterogeneous structural relaxation within the potential energy landscape (PEL) during steepest-descent energy minimization, using order parameters inspired by spin-glass transitions in frustrated magnetic systems. Furthermore, we demonstrate a direct correlation between the population fluctuations of these two states and the anomalous heat capacity observed in supercooled water. We also reveal that the spatial distribution of entropically favored states undergoes a unique crossover near the Widom line, shifting from a spanning network-like cluster to spatially delocalized clusters. Finally, this research links the topography of the PEL to supercooled water's thermodynamic anomalies and introduces new markers for identifying the Widom line in the phase plane, supplementing existing methods based on the maxima of thermodynamic response functions.

We conduct preliminary research on the MORPH-II database, a significant longitudinal face dataset widely used as a benchmark in computer vision and pattern recognition. Initially, we outline the inconsistencies found within the data and detail the cleaning strategies employed, followed by an analysis of how these flaws may have influenced previous studies. Subsequently, we introduce a new automatic subsetting scheme designed to address the unbalanced racial and gender distributions of MORPH-II while maintaining the independence between training and testing sets. Finally, we present a novel global framework for age estimation that leverages posterior probabilities from race classification to generate a composite age estimate. Preliminary experimental results on the MORPH-II dataset are also provided.

Unlike automatic speech recognition (ASR), the human auditory system excels at processing noisy environments, such as those with environmental interference or channel distortion. To replicate this capability, auditory models have been integrated into ASR systems to enhance robustness. This paper introduces a new auditory model that combines psychoacoustics and otoacoustic emissions (OAEs) within ASR frameworks. Specifically, we implement the frequency-dependent characteristics of psychoacoustic models, leading to effective improvements in system performance. Additionally, we propose a novel double-transform spectrum-analysis technique capable of qualitatively predicting ASR performance across various noise types. Detailed theoretical analysis supports the efficacy of the proposed algorithm. Experiments conducted on the AURORA2 database demonstrate that our feature extraction method significantly boosts word recognition rates compared to the baseline. When trained on clean speech, the proposed method achieves up to 85.39% word recognition accuracy on noisy data.

Theoretical predictions and experimental evidence confirm that in-plane compressively strained $\alpha$-Sn films exhibit non-trivial electronic states characteristic of a 3D topological Dirac semimetal. However, the stability of these states is highly sensitive to the material's purity, homogeneity, and structural integrity. We successfully developed a reliable fabrication method to grow pure, strained $\alpha$-Sn films on InSb(100) substrates without applying heat during growth or introducing dopants. Using molecular beam epitaxy, we produced these films and subsequently verified their chemical purity and surface structural properties. Scanning tunneling microscopy provided local details on surface morphology, while Mössbauer spectroscopy confirmed the presence of compressive strain. Notably, the grown samples demonstrated exceptional robustness against ambient conditions. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy validated the topological nature of the samples by revealing the Dirac cone of the topological surface state. Additionally, scanning tunneling spectroscopy offered enhanced insights into the electronic structure of the 3D topological Dirac semimetal $\alpha$-Sn above the Fermi level.

Recent advancements in Natural Language Processing have introduced state-of-the-art Neural Language Models that utilize unsupervised transferable learning through diverse pretraining objectives. Although these models excel in general downstream NLP tasks, their performance on domain-specific applications can be further enhanced through domain adaptation techniques. This study compares and analyzes XLNet (autoregressive) and BERT (autoencoder) on legal tasks. The results indicate that XLNet outperforms other models in the sequence classification task for legal opinions, while BERT achieves superior results in Named Entity Recognition (NER). To further adapt BERT to the legal domain, we employed domain-specific pretraining and incorporated an additional legal vocabulary, creating multiple model variants using both methods individually and in combination. Our analysis reveals that both pretraining and vocabulary enhancements improve BERT's performance on legal opinion classification, while the vocabulary addition specifically boosts NER accuracy. The combination of both techniques yields the best overall results. Consequently, our Legal-Vocab-BERT model achieves the highest performance on the legal opinions task, surpassing larger general pretrained models such as BERT-Base and XLNet-Base.

We first establish that for any compact metrizable space, there exists a topological embedding into the subsets of compact metric spaces characterized by being connected, path-connected, geodesic, or CAT(0) within the Gromov–Hausdorff space, allowing for finite prescribed values. Applying this result, we demonstrate that these specific sets are path-connected and that their non-empty open subsets possess infinite topological dimension. Using the same approach, we further prove that the collection of all proper CAT(0) spaces is path-connected, and its non-empty open subsets exhibit infinite topological dimension under the pointed Gromov–Hausdorff distance.

This work offers a rigorous validation of nonlinear geometric optics expansions for reflecting pulses within space dimensions where $n>1$. These pulses emerge as solutions to variable coefficient semilinear first-order hyperbolic systems. The analysis covers $N\times N$ systems involving $N$ interacting pulses that rely on potentially nonlinear phases. Unlike previous studies, the \emph{coherence} assumption is no longer required. The scope includes scenarios where incoming pulses originate from boundary data, as well as cases where a single outgoing pulse reflects off a possibly curved boundary to generate multiple incoming pulses. While the primary focus is on boundary problems, the methods and results are readily adaptable to the Cauchy problem for $N\times N$ systems in free space.

We present a straightforward stacked configuration that facilitates absorption imaging through an aperture in a grating magneto-optical trap (GMOT) chip, situated directly beneath a micro-fabricated vacuum cell. This imaging method overcomes the challenges of limited optical access and surface scattering inherent to this chip-scale platform, while simultaneously allowing for both atom trapping and imaging using a single incident laser beam. The through-hole imaging technique is employed to assess the effects of the reduced optical overlap volume within the GMOT of the chip-scale cell, with the aim of optimizing atom numbers in low-volume systems.

Variational Bayes (VB) is a foundational technique in machine learning and statistics, driving recent advancements in Bayesian deep learning. Although the natural gradient is vital for efficient VB estimation, its computational cost becomes prohibitive in high-dimensional settings. We introduce a regression-based approach for natural gradient estimation that is computationally efficient and offers convergence guarantees under standard assumptions. This method facilitates the application of quantum matrix inversion to accelerate VB further, as we demonstrate that the proposed setup meets the necessary conditions for such efficiency. Additionally, the approach is applicable across a wide spectrum of statistical models without relying on specialized or simplified variational distributions.

Multiplayer Online Battle Arena (MOBA) games are currently among the most popular genres. As this category expands, there is a growing need to create effective intelligent agents capable of competing with or assisting human players. This paper tackles the challenge of developing agents for MOBA titles by implementing a two-layered architecture that manages both navigation and game mechanics. This system utilizes Influence Maps, a well-established method for tactical analysis. Experiments conducted using {\em League of Legends} as a testbed demonstrate promising outcomes within this highly dynamic real-time environment.

Web archives have expanded to the petabyte scale, offering not only critical insights into social and cultural evolution over the past three decades but also extensive datasets for machine learning. To leverage recent advancements in Deep Learning, these archives necessitate a scalable processing framework capable of supporting both neural network training and inference. Currently, no public library exists to handle web archives in this manner, forcing some applications to rely on makeshift solutions. This paper introduces WARC-DL, a deep learning-integrated pipeline designed for web archive processing that effectively scales to petabyte-level data.

This paper introduces a new virtual-queue-based online algorithm designed for online convex optimization (OCO) problems subject to long-term, time-varying constraints. We provide a performance analysis focusing on dynamic regret and constraint violations, proposing a novel update rule for dual variables and a fresh approach to integrating time-varying constraint functions into these variables. To our knowledge, this is the first parameter-free algorithm to simultaneously achieve sublinear dynamic regret and constraint violations. Our method surpasses current state-of-the-art results in several areas, notably by eliminating the need for the Slater condition. Additionally, for specific practical and well-studied constrained OCO problems where consecutive constraint variations are sufficiently smooth, our algorithm attains $O(1)$ constraint violations. We further extend both the algorithm and its analysis to scenarios with an unknown time horizon $T$. Finally, numerical experiments are presented to verify the theoretical findings, and potential applications of our proposed framework are discussed.

For a family of graphs $\mathcal{H}$, a graph $G$ is defined as $\mathcal{H}$-free if no subset of its vertices induces a subgraph isomorphic to any member of $\mathcal{H}$. This work establishes both necessary and sufficient conditions for a graph $G$ such that contracting any edge $e \in E(G)$ results in an $\mathcal{H}$-free graph. Leveraging these conditions, we provide characterizations for claw-free, matrogenic, and line graphs.

This paper introduces the first deterministic solver for directed Laplacian systems that operates in almost-linear time relative to the number of non-zero entries in the matrix L. Prior reductions now enable the first deterministic almost-linear time algorithms for computing essential directed graph metrics, such as stationary distributions, personalized PageRank, hitting times, and escape probabilities. These advancements rely on a novel method called partial symmetrization, which renders the Laplacian of an Eulerian directed graph "less directed" in a manner that is independently valuable. This approach is effective due to two primary insights: first, the partially symmetrized Laplacian effectively preconditions the original Eulerian Laplacian for Richardson iteration, allowing a solver for the original matrix to be built from one for the symmetrized version; second, the undirected nature of the symmetrized Laplacian permits aggressive sparsification—accepting large spectral errors—while still ensuring Richardson iteration convergence when the sparsified matrix acts as a preconditioner. This capability facilitates the creation of deterministic sparsification tools for the partially symmetrized Laplacian. Combined with existing reductions from directed to Eulerian Laplacians, our method yields the first deterministic almost-linear time algorithm for solving linear equations in directed Laplacians. To underscore the versatility of this technique, we demonstrate that it can derandomize two major existing randomized frameworks for Eulerian Laplacians: the squaring-based approach by Cohen et al. (STOC 2017) and the sparsified Cholesky-based method by Peng and Song (STOC 2022).

Schwarz methods involve dividing a computational domain into subdomains and applying boundary conditions at their interfaces, a process analogous to domain truncation where an unbounded region is restricted to a bounded one with boundary conditions applied at the edges. Viewing Schwarz methods as domain truncations onto subdomains proves beneficial. The first optimal Schwarz method, introduced in 1994, achieved convergence in a finite number of steps by utilizing transparent boundary conditions as transmission rules between subdomains. The approximation of these conditions to ensure rapid convergence gave rise to optimized Schwarz methods—a term now commonly applied to Schwarz approaches based on domain truncation. While classical Schwarz methods, which rely on simple Dirichlet transmission conditions and have proven effective across various applications, are well-established, optimized Schwarz methods remain less understood due to their more complex transmission conditions. This gap in understanding motivates the current survey, which aims to provide a comprehensive review and precise analysis of the convergence behaviors of optimized Schwarz methods through Fourier analysis, considering original boundary conditions, diverse subdomain decompositions, and layered media. The study encompasses transmission conditions ranging from lowest-order absorbing conditions (Robin) to advanced perfectly matched layers (PML), both originally developed for domain truncation.

We demonstrate that for any deterministic top-down transducer equipped with look-ahead, it is decidable whether its translation can be expressed by (1) a linear top-down tree transducer or (2) a tree homomorphism. Furthermore, we provide algorithms that build equivalent transducers of these types whenever they are possible.

We present a proof of factorization for exclusive processes, incorporating soft and collinear modes of arbitrarily low energy that emerge when external lines are placed on-shell. Specifically, we analyze the annihilation of an e⁺e⁻ pair into two light mesons via a virtual photon. In an intermediate stage, we derive a factorized expression featuring a soft function devoid of collinear divergences. This contrasts with soft-collinear effective theory, where low-energy collinear modes naturally factorize directly into the soft function. We highlight that the cancellation of the soft function, which depends on the color-singlet nature of external hadrons, breaks down when the soft function includes low-energy collinear modes.

Community search seeks to identify densely connected subgraphs for specific query vertices within a graph. Although this area has been extensively researched, prior studies predominantly address homogeneous communities, overlooking heterogeneous communities characterized by diverse labels. This paper introduces a novel problem known as the Butterfly-Core Community (BCC) search on labeled graphs, where vertices possess labels denoting their attributes and edges signify cross-relationships between them. Specifically, given two query vertices with distinct labels, the goal is to locate a tightly connected cross-community containing both queries, structured as a collection of butterfly networks. In this structure, each butterfly's wings are formed by k-cores derived from individual query vertices, with the wings linked by these butterflies. The BCC structure ensures structural cohesiveness and a minimal diameter, making it effective for capturing concise, heterogeneous collaborative teams. We provide a theoretical proof that this problem is NP-hard and demonstrate its non-approximability. To address this challenge efficiently, we propose a heuristic algorithm that first identifies a BCC containing the query vertices and then iteratively removes vertices furthest from the queries. This approach achieves a 2-approximation of the optimal solution. Additionally, to enhance efficiency, we introduce a butterfly-core index and develop a suite of algorithms for efficient butterfly-core identification and maintenance during vertex elimination. Comprehensive experiments on eight real-world networks and four new case studies confirm the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed methods.

This study systematically investigates the interaction between the $\phi$ meson and nuclei by analyzing and fitting cross sections of $\gamma N \rightarrow \phi N$ reactions near the threshold, where $N$ denotes the nucleus. Utilizing the vector meson dominance model, we present the energy-dependent distribution of the $\phi$-$N$ scattering length, revealing a marginal increase as energy rises. Combining experimental data with theoretical frameworks, we determine the average $\phi$-proton scattering length to be $0.10\pm0.01$ fm. Furthermore, we derive the average $\phi$-deuteron scattering length for the first time, finding it to be $0.014\pm0.002$ fm. We also examine the impact of the minimum momentum transfer $|t_{min}|$ on the $\phi$-$N$ scattering length at the threshold. These findings offer crucial theoretical insights for a more precise investigation of the $\phi$-$N$ scattering length and establish a foundation for future experimental efforts in $\phi$ meson production.

In the context of generating stereotypes for recommender systems, we observed that specific categorical variables present significant challenges when simple clustering methods are used. A categorical variable is considered complex when it resists easy conversion into numerical form, when the semantic meaning of its categories is crucial for determining optimal stereotypes, and when it involves multiple choices (e.g., items can have one or more applicable categories without a fixed limit). This paper aims to investigate whether a viable recommendation system can be built using stereotypes derived directly from feature metadata similarities, bypassing the use of rating data during the class generation phase. Encouraging results from experiments with integrated MovieLens and Imdb datasets demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms other categorical clustering techniques, such as k-modes, when handling complex categorical features. Furthermore, effectively representing these complex features can help mitigate cold-start problems in recommender systems.

Achieving meaningful differential privacy (DP) security guarantees while training large neural networks remains a significant challenge. This paper addresses the issue by re-examining the two core mechanisms of Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD): iterative perturbation and gradient clipping. We introduce a generic optimization framework named {\em ModelMix}, which achieves random aggregation of intermediate model states. This approach leverages the entropy of the training trajectory to enhance composite privacy analysis, improving $(\epsilon, \delta)$ DP security parameters by an order of magnitude.

We offer rigorous theoretical analyses regarding both the utility and privacy amplification provided by ModelMix. Specifically, we conduct a formal investigation into the impact of gradient clipping within DP-SGD, offering theoretical guidance on hyper-parameter selection. Furthermore, we propose a refined gradient clipping technique that, when integrated with ModelMix, further reduces privacy loss in private learning.

Extensive experiments substantiate our theoretical findings, demonstrating substantial improvements in both privacy and utility. For instance, training a Resnet-20 on CIFAR10 with ModelMix yields $70.4\%$ accuracy under a DP budget of $(\epsilon=8, \delta=10^{-5})$, whereas standard DP-SGD achieves the same accuracy only with $(\epsilon=145.8, \delta=10^{-5})$. Additionally, incorporating public low-dimensional gradient embeddings allows ModelMix to reach $79.1\%$ accuracy with an $(\epsilon=6.1, \delta=10^{-5})$ budget, compared to $(\epsilon=111.2, \delta=10^{-5})$ when using ModelMix-free approaches for equivalent performance.

This study examines a modified $f(R)$ gravity theory within the Palatini framework, incorporating an Holst term coupled with a dynamical Immirzi field. We explore the model's fundamental characteristics, focusing on how the Immirzi field eliminates torsion and interacts with the scalar-tensor degrees of freedom inherent to $f(R)$ gravity. The primary objective is to analyze the morphology of gravitational wave polarizations as they couple to a ring of test particles. Our initial findings reveal that the scalar mode of the $f(R)$ Lagrangian is dynamically frozen because its first-order term vanishes identically. This simplification enables a thorough characterization of the linearized theory, which predicts a modified Newtonian potential in the static limit and, when time dependence is introduced, a standard gravitational wave alongside a scalar wave linked to the Immirzi field. By investigating the interaction of this scalar-tensor wave with a circle of test particles, we define two effective gravitational polarizations that constitute an equivalent phenomenological wave exhibiting anomalous morphology compared to standard General Relativity. Specifically, the test particle ring experiences altered plus and cross modes; these distinct features depend on the model's free parameters and are potentially detectable through data analysis.

We introduce a novel, principled approach to learning a nonparametric graph model known as a graphon, which operates within an infinite-dimensional space to represent graphs of any size. Drawing upon the weak regularity lemma from graphon theory, we utilize a step function to approximate the graphon. We demonstrate that the cut distance between graphons can be relaxed to the Gromov-Wasserstein distance between their respective step functions. Consequently, for a collection of graphs generated by an underlying graphon, we learn the corresponding step function as the Gromov-Wasserstein barycenter of these graphs. Additionally, we develop various enhancements and extensions to the base algorithm, including a smoothed Gromov-Wasserstein barycenter to ensure the continuity of learned graphons, and mixed Gromov-Wasserstein barycenters for learning multiple structured graphons. This proposed method addresses the limitations of previous state-of-the-art techniques and achieves superior performance on both synthetic and real-world datasets. The implementation is accessible at https://github.com/HongtengXu/SGWB-Graphon.

Training machine learning models for land cover semantic segmentation faces a significant disparity between the abundance of satellite imagery available as input and the scarcity of ground truth data required for supervised learning. Although thousands of new satellite images are released daily at no cost, acquiring corresponding ground truth remains difficult, expensive, and time-consuming. This paper introduces "Embedding Earth," a self-supervised contrastive pre-training technique designed to exploit the vast volume of available satellite imagery to enhance performance in downstream dense land cover classification. Through an extensive experimental evaluation across four countries and two continents, we utilized models initialized with our proposed method for supervised land cover semantic segmentation, observing substantial performance gains of up to 25% in absolute mIoU. In all tested scenarios, our approach outperformed random initialization, particularly in data-scarce environments. Ablation studies further reveal that the learned features generalize effectively across diverse regions, suggesting that this pre-training scheme can replace random initialization for Earth observation tasks. The code will soon be available at https://github.com/michaeltrs/DeepSatModels.

This paper establishes the existence of fixed points for mappings satisfying specific asymptotic nonexpansive conditions within Banach spaces characterized by nearly uniform convexity or compact asymptotic centers for bounded sequences. We examine pointwise eventually nonexpansive, pointwise asymptotically nonexpansive, and asymptotically type nonexpansive mappings. Notably, we do not require the mappings to possess continuous iterations, thereby addressing long-standing open questions regarding fixed point existence for such mappings in the absence of continuity.

**Context.** V838 Monocerotis is a unique binary system that experienced a massive stellar outburst in 2002, resulting in an expanding cool supergiant and a B3V hot companion. Five years post-outburst, the B3V star vanished and has yet to reappear. **Aims.** The study examines alterations in the light curve and spectral characteristics. **Methods.** Over the last 13 years, the Nordic Optical Telescope conducted a monitoring campaign to gather optical photometric and spectroscopic data. These datasets were analyzed to determine the temporal evolution of spectral features and the spectral energy distribution, thereby characterizing the object. **Results.** Photometric observations indicate a consistent brightening across all bands over the past 13 years, most notably in the blue spectrum. Spectra confirm this trend with a gradual increase in continuum flux at shorter wavelengths. Additionally, a slow brightening of the H$\alpha$ emission line beginning in 2015 was observed. These shifts suggest the B3V companion may be gradually re-emerging. Simultaneously, the object's observed colors changed significantly, while molecular absorption bands in low-resolution spectra showed a steady reduction in strength and width. These findings imply a rising temperature for the cool supergiant and a weakening of its wind, likely coupled with the secondary star's slow recovery due to dust evaporation and accretion of material from the shell surrounding the hot companion. Analysis of medium-resolution spectra reveals that the heliocentric radial velocity of the TiI atomic absorption line at 6556.06 Å has remained stable for over a decade. We propose that TiI lines trace the velocity of the red supergiant in V838 Mon rather than indicating infalling matter as previously believed.

Kim and Vu proposed a sandwich conjecture for the random $d$-regular graph $\mathcal{G}(n,d)$, asserting that for every $d\gg \log n$, one can find probabilities $p_1=(1-o(1))d/n$ and $p_2=(1+o(1))d/n$ alongside a coupling of three random graphs $(G^L, G, G^U)$ such that marginally $G^L\sim \mathcal{G}(n,p_1)$, $G\sim \mathcal{G}(n,d)$, and $G^U\sim \mathcal{G}(n,p_2)$, while jointly satisfying $P(G^L\subseteq G\subseteq G^U)=1-o(1)$. Recently, Isaev, McKay, and the author validated this conjecture for all $d\gg n/\sqrt{\log n}$ and established a weakened version for $d=O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$ where $p_2$ is approximately $(\log n)\cdot d/n$. This paper demonstrates that the sandwich conjecture remains true for all $d=\omega(\log^7 n)$.

This paper introduces PerspectroScope, a web-based platform that allows users to input a natural language claim worthy of discussion. The system then extracts and visualizes diverse perspectives supporting or opposing that claim, alongside the evidence backing each view, enabling users to explore various facets of the issue. Built upon a combination of retrieval engines and learned textual entailment classifiers utilizing recent advances in natural language understanding, the system also incorporates mechanisms to gather user corrections. These features enhance the platform's adaptability, expand its coverage, and refine its decision-making capabilities over time. PerspectroScope can be accessed at github.com/CogComp/perspectroscope.

Spherical distortion poses a significant obstacle when applying deep learning to omnidirectional imagery, particularly in dense regression tasks like depth estimation where structural integrity is crucial; standard CNN layers applied directly to distorted 360° images often lead to unwanted information loss. To address this, we introduce OmniFusion, a monocular 360° depth estimation framework that converts distorted images into less-distorted perspective patches (tangent images) for individual CNN-based predictions, which are subsequently merged to generate the final output. To resolve the discrepancies between these patch-wise predictions that hinder merging quality, we present a novel framework comprising three key elements: first, a geometry-aware feature fusion mechanism that integrates 2D image features with 3D geometric data to mitigate patch inconsistencies; second, a self-attention-based transformer architecture for global aggregation of patch information to enhance consistency; and third, an iterative depth refinement process that further improves estimated depth using precise geometric features. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach effectively alleviates distortion issues and achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple 360° monocular depth estimation benchmarks.

This paper defines $\eta (G)$ as the count of conjugacy classes of maximal cyclic subgroups within a finite group $G$. We calculate $\eta (G)$ for every metacyclic $p$-group. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for a metacyclic $p$-group of order $p^n$ which is neither dihedral, generalized quaternion, nor semi-dihedral, the inequality $\eta (G) \ge n-2$ holds, and we identify the specific conditions under which equality is achieved.

Rockfalls present a significant danger to ground transport systems due to their speed, destructive capacity, and frequent occurrence on steep terrains adjacent to roads and railways. Assessment strategies for rockfall susceptibility vary from purely phenomenological and statistical approaches, which are ideal for large-scale modeling, to deterministic methods that are more practical for local analyses. A shared necessity in these assessments is identifying potential detachment points, typically located on cliffs uphill, and evaluating the subsequent runout zones. In this study, we utilize a physically based model to simulate rockfall trajectories across the entire Italian railway network, covering a corridor approximately 17,000 km long with varying widths. We introduce a data-driven approach to pinpoint rockfall source points by employing expert mapping of potential source areas at representative sample sites. By utilizing empirical distributions of gridded slope values from these expert-mapped source zones, we generated probabilistic maps of rockfall sources near the railway network, independent of specific triggers. These source areas serve as the initiation points for trajectory simulations within the three-dimensional STONE model. This program delivers a pixel-by-pixel trajectory count spanning 24,500 km², representing the largest homogeneous application of the model to date. We categorized the results into a vector susceptibility map for railway segments, providing segment-specific susceptibility assessments. Furthermore, by adopting a graph representation of the network, we classified segments based on both their rockfall susceptibility and their functional role within the network, yielding a network-ranked susceptibility. Both maps are instrumental for future hazard evaluations and for prioritizing safety enhancements along the railway at a national level.

For a convex body $K\subset \mathbb R^2$, a circle $\Omega\subset \text{int} \ K$ is defined as an equipotential circle if every tangent line to $\Omega$ intersects $K$ in a chord $AB$ such that, at the contact point $P=\Omega\cap AB$, the product $|AP|\cdot|PB|$ equals a constant $\lambda$. The primary finding of this article states that if a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ possesses an equipotential circle $\mathcal B$ with center $O$ in its interior, then $K$ must be symmetric about $O$. Furthermore, unless any chord of $K$ tangent to $\mathcal B$ subtends an angle of $\pi/2$ at $O$, $K$ is necessarily a disc. Additionally, the study presents results characterizing ellipsoids and spheres in $\mathbb R^3$ and introduces the notion of an equireciprocal disc.

Most Named Entity Recognition (NER) models rely on the assumption that training data is fully annotated. Although this holds true for standard datasets like CoNLL 2003 and OntoNotes, acquiring complete annotations is often impractical, particularly when entities are selectively labeled to reduce costs. This study introduces a method for fine-tuning BERT on such partially labeled datasets by leveraging self-supervision and label preprocessing. Our technique surpasses prior LSTM-based preprocessing baselines, yielding significant performance gains on sparsely annotated data. Furthermore, we show that applying this approach while fine-tuning RoBERTa on the CoNLL 2003 dataset with only 10% entity labeling achieves results comparable to a baseline model trained with 50% labeling.

Hadronic resonances serve as probes for the late-stage hadron gas in heavy-ion collisions because their lifetimes, ranging from 1 to 10 fm/$c$, align with the system's decoupling time. Within this gas, elastic and inelastic scatterings of decay products that occurred prior to kinetic freeze-out compete with regeneration processes, with the net outcome determined by resonance lifetimes, the duration of the hadronic phase, and relevant cross-sections. Notably, the $\Sigma(1385)^{\pm}$ particle is significant because models suggest regeneration outweighs rescattering despite its short lifetime of approximately 5.5 fm/$c$. This Letter presents the initial measurement of $\Sigma(1385)^{\pm}$ production at midrapidity in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}= 5.02$ TeV using the ALICE detector. Reconstructed through their $\Lambda\pi$ hadronic decay channel, the resonances are analyzed across transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) and collision centrality. The findings are compared against pion yields, statistical hadronization model predictions, and simulations from event generators such as PYTHIA8/Angantyr and EPOS3 coupled with the UrQMD afterburner. No model successfully reproduces the data. Furthermore, the observed behavior of $\Sigma(1385)^{\pm}$ mirrors that of ${\rm K}^{*} (892)^{0}$, a result that contradicts the predictions of EPOS3 with an afterburner.

We develop two rational approximate solutions for the Thomas-Fermi (TF) nonlinear differential equation, derived by applying the principle of dynamic consistency. Beyond analyzing the discrepancies in the numerical predictions of these two solutions, we evaluate them against a precise numerical solution generated via a fourth-order Runge-Kutta method. Furthermore, we introduce several novel integral relations that hold true for the bounded solutions of the TF equation.

Recent research has increasingly investigated the application of neural networks to various routing challenges, representing a promising field. Typically, these studies employ an encoder-decoder architecture that generates node sequences (paths) by combining node embeddings with problem-specific context, followed by beam search optimization. However, current models are limited by their reliance solely on node coordinates, their neglect of the self-referential nature of routing tasks, and their insufficient attention to the unreliability of early node selections, hindering their practical application.

This paper addresses these shortcomings using the orienteering problem as a case study. We introduce a novel approach combining a modified beam search algorithm with a learned heuristic to solve the general orienteering problem. The heuristic is derived from an attention network that processes inter-node distances and is trained via a reinforcement learning framework. Empirical results demonstrate that our method outperforms numerous baselines and achieves performance comparable to optimal or highly specialized solutions. Furthermore, our framework is adaptable to other routing problems, and the source code is publicly accessible.

The efficacy of vehicle active safety systems relies heavily on the friction generated at the tire-road interface; consequently, accurately determining the tire-road friction coefficient is critical for optimizing various vehicle control strategies. This study addresses the estimation of this friction coefficient by leveraging lateral tire force data. A Time Delay Neural Network (TDNN) is utilized for the proposed estimation framework, which identifies road friction levels during lateral force excitations without relying on conventional mathematical tire models, thereby offering a more efficient and robust solution. Furthermore, the method estimates friction independently for each wheel, bypassing the simplifications associated with lumped axle models. To validate the proposed approach, simulations using a realistic vehicle model were conducted across diverse road surfaces and driving maneuvers. The outcomes were benchmarked against a classical method and a model-based nonlinear regression technique.

This study addresses the well-established challenge of morphing attacks, a topic of significant interest within the biometrics field. Such attacks exploit vulnerabilities in face recognition systems, leading to false acceptances that pose severe risks, particularly to national security. To counter these threats, we introduce a detection method grounded in a discriminative 2D Discrete Wavelet Transform (2D-DWT). By analyzing specific wavelet sub-bands, our approach highlights inconsistencies between genuine and morphed images. We identified a notable disparity in the entropy values of corresponding sub-bands across real and morphed samples. Leveraging this difference, we calculated the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the entropy distributions of authentic and morphed images. Sub-bands exhibiting the highest KL-divergence were deemed the most discriminative; consequently, we selected 22 such sub-bands for morph detection. A Deep Neural Network (DNN) trained on these 22 features demonstrated high precision in identifying morphed images. Furthermore, our algorithm's efficacy was confirmed through experiments on three datasets: VISAPP17, LMA, and MorGAN. Additionally, we conducted an ablation study to evaluate the impact of sub-band selection.

This letter introduces joint sampling and transmission scheduling policies that are optimal regarding query age for a heterogeneous status update system featuring a stochastic arrival source, a generate-at-will source, and an unreliable channel. The primary objective is to minimize the average query age of information (QAoI) while adhering to constraints on average sampling, average transmission, and per-slot transmission limits. To achieve this, we formulate and solve an optimization problem by converting it into a linear program. Additionally, we present a low-complexity near-optimal policy based on weakly coupled constrained Markov decision processes. Numerical results indicate that the proposed policies yield up to a 32% performance improvement over a benchmark policy.

Dipole models that depend on the impact parameter serve as excellent instruments for probing the proton's spatial configuration. By analyzing the incoherent $ep$ cross section in exclusive $J/\psi$ photoproduction from HERA measurements, we observe that as $|t|$ grows, these models require incorporating multiple levels of substructure within gluon density fluctuations to accurately fit the data. Rather than relying on a perturbative framework, we manually introduce this substructure, conceptualizing it as "hotspots within hotspots." This approach allows for the description of measurements where $|t|> 1$~GeV$^2$, a requirement essential for analyzing observables that integrate over the $t$-spectrum, such as rapidity or $W_{\gamma p}$. We determine that three tiers of proton substructure suffice to provide a robust description of all accessible $ep$ data up to $|t|=30~$GeV$^2$. Furthermore, we note that the structure of gluonic density fluctuations exhibits scaling behavior; specifically, the logarithms of the hotspot count and their dimensions align linearly, thereby significantly narrowing the model's parameter space. Ultimately, these results systematically constrain the model and offer a benchmark for advancing a perturbative description of spatial gluon fluctuations within nucleons.

Extracting relevant passages from extensive documents demands a sophisticated grasp of both discourse and broader document context. We address this challenge within a clinical setting, focusing on how physicians identify patient cohorts based on diagnoses and other underlying medical factors. We present CAPR, a rule-based self-supervised objective designed to train Transformer language models for domain-specific passage matching. Furthermore, we provide a new retrieval dataset constructed from clinical notes to emulate this scenario across a large corpus. We implemented our objective using four Transformer-based architectures: Contextual Document Vectors, Bi-encoders, Poly-encoders, and Cross-encoders. Through extensive evaluation on MIMIC-III and three additional healthcare datasets, we demonstrate that CAPR surpasses strong baselines in retrieving domain-specific passages and generalizes effectively across both rule-based and human-labeled data. Consequently, the model proves particularly potent in zero-shot scenarios where training data is scarce.

Sentence embeddings are a vital element of numerous natural language processing (NLP) systems. Similar to word embeddings, they are generally trained on extensive text corpora and subsequently applied to downstream tasks like retrieval and clustering. However, unlike word embeddings, the most effective sentence embedding methods rely on labeled data, restricting their applicability to languages and domains where such data is plentiful. This paper introduces DeCLUTR: Deep Contrastive Learning for Unsupervised Textual Representations. Drawing inspiration from recent breakthroughs in deep metric learning, we develop a self-supervised objective designed to learn universal sentence embeddings without needing labeled training data. When employed to extend the pretraining of transformer-based language models, our method narrows the performance divide between unsupervised and supervised pretraining for universal sentence encoders. Crucially, our experiments indicate that the quality of the resulting embeddings increases with both the number of trainable parameters and the volume of unlabeled training data. We have made our code and pretrained models publicly accessible, allowing for easy adaptation to new domains or the embedding of unseen text.

The creation of precise and scalable cross-modal image-text retrieval systems, capable of matching queries from one domain (such as text) to archives in another (like remote sensing imagery), has garnered significant interest within the remote sensing community. However, most current approaches rely on the assumption that reliable training datasets with perfectly aligned text-image pairs are available. This assumption is often flawed, as these datasets frequently contain noisy pairs where captions do not accurately describe the images, thereby distorting the retrieval models' learning process. To overcome this challenge, we introduce CHNR, a novel unsupervised cross-modal hashing framework designed to be robust against noisy image-text correspondences. CHNR comprises three components: a feature extraction module to derive representations from image-text pairs, a noise detection module to identify unreliable correspondences, and a hashing module to produce cross-modal binary codes. The framework operates through two distinct training stages: first, a meta-learning phase that employs a small set of clean data to train the noise detector using an adversarial approach; second, the main training phase, where the trained detector filters noisy pairs while the hashing module is optimized on the full noisy dataset. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that CHNR surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods. The source code is publicly accessible at https://git.tu-berlin.de/rsim/chnr.

Software developers often face numerous change requests from users during maintenance, and research indicates that identifying suitable search terms for concept location within these requests is particularly difficult. This paper introduces QUICKAR, a novel approach that automatically generates beneficial query reformulations by utilizing crowdsourced data from Stack Overflow. The method evaluates the semantic similarity or relevance between terms by examining their adjacent word contexts within programming questions on the platform, subsequently proposing semantically related queries to aid concept location. Empirical results from 510 queries across two software systems demonstrate that QUICKAR can enhance or maintain the quality of approximately 76% of initial queries on average, a promising outcome. Furthermore, comparisons with a baseline technique validate these preliminary findings and highlight the method's potential.

This study aims to synthesize existing literature on Koopman-von Neumann (KvN) Mechanics into an accessible and straightforward text. As a branch of classical mechanics reformulated using the mathematical framework of quantum mechanics, KvN Mechanics employs a Hilbert phase space and operators to compute the expectation values of key observables, such as position and momentum. Serving as a vital instrument in statistical physics and offering insight into the enigmatic connection between classical and quantum realms, this field has seen the development of numerous significant applications over the past decade.

Wrinkle formation is a prevalent issue when expanding two-dimensional layered materials across large areas on metallic substrates. Since these wrinkles can substantially impact the functionality of large-scale electronic devices based on 2D materials, it is critical to examine their local electrical characteristics. In this study, we present local conductivity data obtained via conducting atomic force microscopy (CAFM) and surface potential maps generated by Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy (KPFM) on extensive wrinkled turbostratic graphene films grown on nickel foils. Our findings demonstrate that electrical transport currents on wrinkles exceed those on flat regions by several orders of magnitude. Consequently, our results indicate that the deliberate engineering of such wrinkles in graphene could enable the creation of advanced graphene-based nano-electronic devices designed for high-current transport through narrow channels.

The primary component of the vanilla Vision Transformer (ViT) is the attention mechanism, which enables the model to capture global context from input images. While ViTs achieve superior performance with large-scale datasets, their data-intensive requirements have led to the development of hybrid-ViT architectures that incorporate local context to mitigate this limitation. Unlike Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), the robustness of ViTs and their variants against adversarial attacks remains underexplored in existing literature. This study investigates three aspects of ViT robustness: 1) performance against various $L_p$-based adversarial attacks compared to CNNs, 2) resilience under adversarial examples following preprocessing defense techniques, and 3) vulnerability to adaptive attacks utilizing the Expectation Over Transformation (EOT) framework. Experiments conducted on 1,000 ImageNet-1k images reveal that both vanilla ViTs and hybrid-ViTs demonstrate greater robustness than CNNs. Specifically, vanilla ViTs and hybrid-ViTs outperform CNNs under both $L_p$-based and adaptive attacks. However, unlike hybrid-ViTs, vanilla ViTs do not benefit from preprocessing defenses that primarily attenuate high-frequency components. To deepen the understanding of these attention-based models, the study provides joint analyses of feature maps, attention maps, and Grad-CAM visualizations alongside image quality metrics and perturbation energy spectra.

We formulate nonlinear wave equations that model the propagation of slowly varying wavepackets composed of topological valley-Hall edge states. Our analysis demonstrates that edge pulses undergo fragmentation even without spatial dispersion, driven by nonlinear self-steepening. This self-steepening induces a previously overlooked gradient catastrophe that arises within a finite time scale defined by the ratio of the pulse's nonlinear frequency shift to the magnitude of the topological band gap. Incorporating weak spatial dispersion subsequently yields stable edge quasi-solitons. These results are broadly applicable to systems governed by Dirac-like Hamiltonians and are confirmed through numerical simulations of pulse propagation along a valley-Hall domain wall in staggered honeycomb waveguide lattices exhibiting Kerr nonlinearity.

Generating and acquiring digital human avatars is a critical challenge with significant applications in virtual telepresence, gaming, and human modeling. Current avatar generation methods generally fall into two categories: 3D-based approaches that utilize multi-view data to construct 3D representations (such as meshes, implicit surfaces, or volumes) with appearance, and 2D-based methods that produce photo-realistic images but fail to provide accurate 3D geometry. This paper introduces DRaCoN, a framework designed to learn full-body volumetric avatars by leveraging the strengths of both 2D and 3D neural rendering. DRaCoN comprises a Differentiable Rasterization module (DiffRas), which synthesizes a low-resolution target image alongside latent features guided by a parametric body model. This output conditions a subsequent conditional neural 3D representation module (c-NeRF), which generates high-resolution images and precise body geometry through volumetric rendering. While DiffRas ensures photo-realistic image quality, c-NeRF utilizes signed distance fields (SDFs) to capture fine 3D geometric details. Experiments on the challenging ZJU-MoCap and Human3.6M datasets demonstrate that DRaCoN surpasses state-of-the-art methods in both error metrics and visual fidelity.

Federated learning (FL) has enabled privacy-preserving deep learning across diverse applications, including medical image classification and network intrusion detection. However, FL relies on a central parameter server for model aggregation, which introduces communication delays and susceptibility to adversarial attacks. In contrast, fully decentralized architectures like Swarm Learning facilitate peer-to-peer communication among distributed nodes without requiring a central server. A primary challenge in decentralized deep learning is the non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) nature of data across nodes, which often leads to slow model convergence. To address this, we introduce Homogeneous Learning (HL), a decentralized model designed to handle non-IID data using a self-attention mechanism. In HL, training occurs on a selected node per round, with the trained model being transmitted to the next selected node at the end of each round. Specifically, the selection process employs a self-attention mechanism powered by reinforcement learning to analyze a node's internal state and its surrounding environment to determine the optimal node for selection. We evaluated HL in various scenarios for image classification, and the results indicate that it outperforms standalone learning. Furthermore, compared to random policy-based decentralized learning for non-IID data, HL reduces total training rounds by 50.8% and communication costs by 74.6%.

Although Siamese-based trackers have achieved significant success, their performance remains unsatisfactory in complex scenarios, particularly in the presence of distractors. To address this, we introduce a novel Siamese relation network featuring two efficient modules: the Relation Detector (RD) and the Refinement Module (RM). The RD employs a meta-learning approach to develop the capability of filtering distractors from the background, while the RM effectively integrates RD into the Siamese framework to produce precise tracking outcomes. Furthermore, to enhance the tracker's discriminability and robustness, we implement a contrastive training strategy that simultaneously learns to match identical targets and distinguish between different objects. Consequently, our tracker delivers accurate results even when encountering background clutter, rapid motion, and occlusion. Experimental evaluations across five prominent benchmarks—VOT2018, VOT2019, OTB100, LaSOT, and UAV123—demonstrate that the proposed method is highly effective, achieving state-of-the-art performance. The source code will be accessible at https://github.com/hqucv/siamrn.

Loneliness is linked to adverse physical and mental health consequences, making it essential to understand how individuals express and manage various types of loneliness. This knowledge is crucial for early detection and targeted interventions, especially for vulnerable populations like young adults. To investigate how different loneliness forms and coping mechanisms appear in self-disclosures, we created the FIG-Loneliness (FIne-Grained Loneliness) dataset using Reddit posts from two young adult-specific forums and two broader loneliness-related forums with a diverse age range. Trained human annotators provided binary and fine-grained labels for these posts. Two BERT-based models, trained on FIG-Loneliness, were then employed to analyze loneliness types and authors' coping strategies within these forums. The binary classification model achieved over 97% accuracy, while the fine-grained classification reached an average accuracy of 77% across all categories. Using FIG-Loneliness and model predictions, we discovered that loneliness expressions in young adult forums differ significantly from those in other forums; young adults were more likely to voice concerns about peer relationships and showed heightened sensitivity to geographical isolation caused by COVID-19 lockdowns. Furthermore, our findings indicate that different forms of loneliness are associated with distinct coping strategies.

This paper establishes several theorems regarding value distribution, which subsequently yield normality criteria for families of analytic functions, thereby extending and improving upon recent findings in the field.

While Stefan Kopp and Nicole Kramer (2021) acknowledge that, despite impressive progress over the last decade, creating computers capable of even moderately human-like conversation remains unsolved, they identify the necessary skills as incremental joint co-construction and mentalizing. Although this paper fully endorses their diagnosis of the problem, it advocates for a distinct solution grounded in the "new" AI framework of situated action.

This study examines the linear stability of a sinusoidal shear flow under an initially uniform streamwise magnetic field within the framework of incompressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) accounting for finite resistivity and viscosity. While this flow is recognized as unstable to the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability in both hydrodynamics and ideal MHD (where dissipation is ignored, provided the magnetic field remains below a critical stabilizing threshold), we show that incorporating viscosity and resistivity yields two novel instability modes. The first, termed a resistively-unstable Alfvén wave owing to its link with shear Alfvén waves, emerges for any non-zero magnetic field strength when the magnetic Prandtl number $Pm < 1$. We develop a reduced model identifying the excitation mechanism as the negative eddy viscosity inherent in periodic shear flows, as described by Dubrulle & Frisch (1991). Furthermore, numerical simulations reveal that this mode saturates into a quasi-stationary state characterized by counter-propagating solitons.

Real-world datasets are predominantly unlabeled or contain very few labeled instances. Since manual annotation is costly and labor-intensive, there is a strong need for unsupervised learning methods capable of matching the performance of supervised or semi-supervised approaches. Contrastive self-supervised learning has recently emerged as a promising solution, sometimes even surpassing supervised techniques. In this study, we introduce SelfGNN, a novel contrastive self-supervised graph neural network (GNN) that operates without explicit contrastive terms. Instead, we utilize Batch Normalization to introduce implicit contrastive mechanisms without compromising performance. Recognizing that data augmentation is critical for contrastive learning, we propose four feature augmentation (FA) strategies specifically designed for graphs. While topological augmentation (TA) is common, our empirical results indicate that FA performs comparably to TA. Furthermore, unlike TA, which often suffers from O(N³) time complexity where N is the number of nodes, FA incurs no additional computational overhead. Evaluations across seven public real-world datasets demonstrate that SelfGNN is highly effective, achieving performance on par with state-of-the-art supervised GNNs and consistently outperforming current semi-supervised and unsupervised GNNs. The source code is accessible at https://github.com/zekarias-tilahun/SelfGNN.

The distinct developmental and operational traits of machine learning (ML) components, combined with their intrinsic uncertainties, necessitate robust engineering principles to guarantee quality. Our objective is to identify how software systems can be re-architected to facilitate the reliable integration of ML elements. To achieve this, we executed a mixed-methods empirical study comprising: (i) a systematic literature review to uncover existing challenges and solutions in ML software architecture; (ii) semi-structured interviews with practitioners to qualitatively expand upon initial findings; and (iii) a survey to quantitatively verify these challenges and solutions. We identified and validated twenty challenges and corresponding strategies for architecting systems with ML components. Our findings suggest that while traditional architectural issues (e.g., component coupling) remain significant, they coexist with novel ML-specific hurdles (e.g., the requirement for continuous retraining). Furthermore, the study reveals that ML-driven decision factors, such as privacy, hold less weight compared to conventional drivers like scalability. By leveraging survey data, we established a connection between architectural solutions and software quality attributes, thereby defining twenty tactical approaches to meet specific quality requirements in ML-enabled systems. Collectively, these results form an empirical framework to support the re-architecting of software systems incorporating ML components.

In the Correlated Gaussian Method, Gaussian basis function parameters are typically selected stochastically via pseudo-random sequences. We demonstrate that utilizing alternative low-discrepancy sequences, or quasi-random sequences, results in bases of superior quality.

The uneven distribution of local data across various edge devices (clients) leads to diminished accuracy and slower training speeds in federated learning. While standard federated learning strategies and many existing alternatives attempt to enhance fairness by weighting the aggregation of deep learning models, this study introduces a novel form of non-IID data known as cluster-skew. In this scenario, groups of clients possess local data with similar distributions, causing the global model to converge toward an over-fitted solution. To address non-IID data, particularly cluster-skewed distributions, we propose FedDRL, a new federated learning framework that utilizes deep reinforcement learning to adaptively calculate each client's impact factor, which serves as the weight in the aggregation process. Comprehensive experiments across multiple federated datasets demonstrate that FedDRL significantly outperforms FedAvg and FedProx methods; for instance, on the CIFAR-100 dataset, it achieves average improvements of up to 4.05% and 2.17%, respectively.

Recent research has demonstrated that a viscosity gradient can induce electrical current within a negatively charged nanochannel (Wiener and Stein, arXiv:1807.09106). To elucidate the physics behind this effect, we utilized the Maxwell-Stefan equation to establish a relationship between solvent flux and driving forces. Our one-dimensional model, applicable to both ideal and non-ideal solvents, indicates that ionic current is influenced by solvent ideality; however, both cases align well with experimental observations.
